#4967. Fall Weddings Are More Popular Than Ever. Here's How to Dress for One (The Right Way)

Autumn is now the most popular season to tie the knot.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

WEDDINGS CAN be hard to dress for, and this isn’t limited to those directly involved; being a mere attendant requires some degree of planning. I’ve attended quite a few weddings over the last year, both as a groomsman and as a regular guest, both with their own sartorial challenges. (I actually found it more stressful not being in the wedding party, at least in one aspect: I had to pick out my own outfit. This also allowed for a little creativity.)

I covered some options for summer weddings a few months back, and just like that, we’re on to the next season. Fall has arguably become the season for weddings; in fact, October recently overtook June as the most popular month for weddings in the U.S. I can attest to this; I was in two separate ones last October.

Summer and fall weddings have quite a few differences. You can get away with some more “fun” looks in the summer, and you can get a little more creative with the materials (linen, seersucker, etc.). Fall weddings are typically a little more buttoned-up, but there’s a little wiggle room there, too.

I’ll go through some of the easiest ways for guys to dress for an autumn affair—with different wedding types in mind—to get you off the ground. We also included plenty of price points because, as everyone knows, weddings can get expensive fast.

Brooks Brothers Explorer Collection Non-Iron Twill Button Down Collar

Cole Haan Men's Grand Neoclassic Plain Toe Oxfords

We’ll start with what we consider a traditional wedding: a separate ceremony at a church, chapel, or the wedding venue without a black-tie dress code. This is about as classic as it gets, so you don’t have to go overboard—but we do recommend wearing a timeless suit. Our style team has tested plenty of affordable menswear brands offering solid options that approximate the look and fit of made-to-measure tailoring. One of them is the Black Tux, an upstart that offers suits for both rental and purchase, with virtual and in-person fittings to match you with the closest standard size. The prices are great, too: the Essential Suit is just under $300 all in. We also happened to score a 20 percent off code for the Black Tux, made exclusively for Men’s Health readers. Just use code MH20 at checkout (minimum of $295). The code’s good until October 31. Most of its higher-priced suits also include a rental option, but for the extra $100 or so, we’d recommend just buying one. The True Navy is a safe color you can wear year-round. The Grey Suit is a step up and is made from a heavier—but still breathable—merino wool. Perfect for the autumn temperatures.

A classic dress shirt is more than okay, but if you want to stand out in an otherwise pretty basic look, you can go with a classic twill dress shirt like this one from Brooks Brothers. You can get a little bit more creative with the tie, but nothing too crazy; the left-to-right diagonal stripes of a classic rep tie keep it distinguished. A Classic Textured Solid Tie is always a safe bet, too. Baby blue and pink go well with a gray suit, and navy, black, and red look better with gray. The shoes are easy, too: black plain-toe oxfords for grays, and these simple brown Astorflex Loafers with a crisp navy blue.

Brooks Brothers Classic Fit Double-Breasted Wool Pinstripe 1818 Suit

Charles Tyrwhitt Cotton Pocket Square - White

Mack Weldon Silver Extended Crew Dress Sock

The Black Tux Picture Frame Brushed Gold Tie Bar

Black-tie affairs probably require even less creativity, but there are definitely ways to push the envelope to stand out. The safe choice, of course, is the classic tux. If you plan to need one on multiple occasions, we also love that the Black Tux once again gets top marks; its Essential option is also under $300. There are some pricier options you can also rent, but the Essential Tux is low-key enough to rock at any formal occasion. SuitShop is another upstart offering ready-to-wear tuxedos at accessible prices, including several options under $300. Accessories-wise, you can opt for a super fancy pair of onyx cufflinks from one of our favorite watch brands, Shinola, but something a little more budget-friendly is more than okay.

Nowadays, you don’t have to go all-black, at least depending on the event. But if you do deviate, you'd better make it count. Like upgrading to a double-breasted suit, for example. The Classic Fit Double-Breasted Wool Pinstripe 1818 Suit elevates your look without making you look like a Prohibition-era mobster (surprisingly, a very fine line).

The other big component of all of this: your shoes. You probably don’t want to go with a loafer; an oxford or derby shoe is the better option. Our favorite: Cole Haan’s Hawthorne Oxfords, a classic dress shoe that’s made with the brand’s famously comfortable insoles so your dogs will stay happy for hours. It’s also versatile enough to wear at dressy events or in a more casual office vibe. In other words, you’ll be getting a lot of use out of it.

If you want to go all out, you can go full custom. Go big or go home, as they say. If you’re in the NYC area, Alan David Custom is a great choice. The bespoke tailor will give you a sample suit to try on before making final decisions, and the experience is a throwback to classier times. They’ll even ship it to you when it’s all said and done. If you want to go fully custom, you’ll also need the shoes to match.

Bonobos Empire Stretch Italian Wool Tuxedo

Todd Snyder Italian Lightweight Sutton Jacket

Quince Supima Cotton Herringbone Dress Shirt

Todd Snyder Relaxed Fit Japanese Selvedge Chino

Reigning Champ Stretch Chino Marina Standard Pant

Allen Edmonds Rhett Cap-toe Oxford Dress Shoe

Cocktail weddings give you a little more freedom than a traditional one. Here, you can rock a classic suit or a nice blazer and slacks, and you wouldn’t be wrong either way. The classic Ludlow tux from J.Crew gives off serious old-school cocktail jacket vibes, and it’s reserved for swankier occasions. Todd Snyder’s Italian Lightweight Sutton Jacket is another high-end option that’s both breathable and easy to wear throughout the night. If you wear blazers regularly, you’ll also get plenty of use out of this, even into the hotter months. Todd Snyder also makes our favorite pair of relaxed-fit chinos that check a lot of boxes for us. The Relaxed Fit Japanese Selvedge Chino is a steep departure from the ones we wear to the office, which is why it’s such a legit option for dressier occasions.

If the baggier fit (and higher price tag) is scaring you off a bit, Reigning Champ makes an ultra-breathable cotton-twill chino that wears more like a standard dress pant. They’re comfortable, breathable, and have a little added stretch; you’ll get a lot of use out of them outside the wedding. The other big component of all of this: your shoes. You probably don’t want to go with a loafer; an Oxford or derby shoe is the better option. Our style team loves Allen Edmonds’. It’s made with calfskin leather, with a surprisingly light-yet-cushioned outsole that’s comfortable enough to use all night.

Billy Reid Exploded Glen Plaid Archie Jacket

Brooks Brothers Straight-Fit Cotton Advantage Chino Pants

Brooks Brothers Friday Shirt, Oxford Patterns

Madewell Johnny-Collar Sweater Polo in Slub Knit Cotton

Cole Haan Zerogrand Remastered Wing Tip Oxford

Barns have since had a huge come-up and are now a hugely popular wedding venue. Regardless of your stance on barn weddings, you have to dress a little differently. Vineyard weddings (and really any outdoor event) live in that same category. If you’re looking at a late-fall event, you’ll want something a little warmer. The Grey Plaid Wool Suit is a step up in that department without being too overbearing; the subtle designs also scream fall. You can also go with the blazer-and-dress-pants route. Abercrombie’s A&F Collins Blazer is a fantastic budget option, and the Olive Stripe colorway similarly gives off fall vibes. It’s easy to pair with dressier chinos, like the Straight-Fit Cotton Advantage Chino Pants from Brooks Brothers. They’re essentially dress pants with a certain chinoesque comfort.

If you do go this route, you can have a little fun with the undershirt; Brooks Brothers’ Friday Shirt can add some flair to your getup. Madewell’s Johnny-Collar Sweater Polo is also a nice departure from your traditional button-down (and a lot more comfortable, too). If the wedding isn’t all that fancy, you can get away with rocking some of the most comfortable dress shoes/sneakers out there: Cole Haan’s Zerogrand Remastered Wing Tip Oxfords.

Buck Mason Capitola Linen Carry-On Jacket

Bonobos Stretch Weekday Warrior Dress Pants

Reigning Champ Heavyweight Jersey OG T-Shirt

The destination wedding can definitely be a challenge, depending on how close you are to the person (or people) getting married. They’re always a great time, though, and you can get similarly creative. We suggest a travel blazer; you’re already shelling out a lot of money for flights and accommodations, so you can save a few bucks by not checking a full suit. Our style director, Christian Gollayan, recently did a full review of the Bonobos Jetsetter Knit Blazer. He described it as a “lifesaver” when traveling. You can definitely rock it at a fall destination wedding, especially considering the hardworking knit construction. #4966. Tom Lee Blames Nvidia and Anthropic IPO for Ethereum Plunge as Bitmine Buys the Dip

Tom Lee Blames Nvidia and Anthropic IPO for Ethereum Plunge as Bitmine Buys the Dip

Bitmine Immersion Technologies kept buying Ethereum through a punishing selloff, adding 7,653 ETH worth roughly $14 million, as chairman Tom Lee argued the token’s steep decline runs counter to improving fundamentals and echoes a dip that preceded a major tech IPO earlier this year.

The NYSE-listed company said Monday its holdings reached 6,077,745 ETH, worth about $11.1 billion at a reference price of $1,823 per coin, far below where the firm’s stack was valued just weeks ago.

That marks a stark drop in paper value: Bitmine’s total crypto, cash and “moonshot” holdings now stand at $11.8 billion, down from $14.3 billion a week earlier, almost entirely because of ETH’s price slide rather than any selling.

The position still represents 4.97% of Ethereum’s 122.2 million token supply, leaving Bitmine 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5% of the network, the target it calls the “Alchemy of 5%.”

Lee did not sugarcoat the move. “ETH tumbled 28% in the past two weeks,” he said, calling the “waterfall decline” inconsistent with what he views as positive fundamentals, including banks and financial institutions announcing tokenization projects built on Ethereum. (Disclosure: Tom Lee is an investor in Dastan, Decrypt’s parent company.)

He pointed to external pressures weighing on the price, including the fallout from Nvidia’s turmoil triggering margin selling in Asia and investors raising cash ahead of Anthropic’s initial public offering, whose pricing is reported for Nov. 18.

Lee also drew a historical parallel, arguing the drop mirrors the sell-off ahead of SpaceX’s $75 billion June IPO, when ETH fell 39% over eight weeks and bottomed three trading days before pricing. Lee suggested the current slump, down a similar amount ahead of the Anthropic listing, could follow the same pattern.

Bitmine remains the world’s largest Ethereum treasury and the second-largest crypto treasury overall, behind Michael Saylor’s Strategy, which now holds 849,327 BTC. Strategy also kept buying through the downturn, with Saylor nudging the market to rally with the quip “this dip could use a little orange.”

Bitmine has 5,227,037 ETH, about 86% of its holdings, staked through its MAVAN platform, with projected annualized revenue of roughly $245 million at current levels.

It also holds 216 Bitcoin, $448 million in cash and marketable securities, a $180 million stake in Beast Industries and a $67 million position in Eightco Holdings.

#4963. Safe wallet reportedly loses $6.5M as Zodiac suspects key compromise

Zodiac’s co-founder said a likely compromised key and overly permissive wallet settings enabled the theft, rather than a flaw in its smart contracts.

A Safe wallet reportedly lost about $6.45 million in cryptocurrency Monday, with Zodiac’s co-founder pointing to a likely compromised key and the wallet’s permissions settings rather than a flaw in Zodiac’s contracts.

Blockchain security firm PeckShield reported the suspected theft, citing onchain investigator Specter. Ethereum blockchain records reviewed by Cointelegraph show that approximately 4.39 million USDC (USDC) and 1.72 million syrupUSDC tokens were transferred from the wallet in a single transaction on Monday.

Johannes Moormann, co-founder of Zodiac, told Cointelegraph that his team reviewed the transaction and confirmed it passed through the wallet’s Zodiac Roles Modifier, which checked the transfer against its configured permissions policy and allowed it. “There is no vulnerability in the module. The contracts worked correctly. The transaction came from the key of a long-standing role member, which was most likely compromised,” he said.

Moormann added that the wallet’s custom permissions policy permitted the transaction, almost certainly unintentionally. He said the wallet’s operators controlled its keys and permissions, and that Zodiac had neither access to them nor involvement in the setup. Zodiac has not been in contact with the affected team.

Specter first flagged the Zodiac Roles module as part of the suspected attack. PeckShield also said the attacker used approximately $813,000 to purchase Monero-linked tokens on Hyperliquid.

The Zodiac Roles module allows Safe users to assign permissions for specific transactions. Moormann said the incident did not indicate a vulnerability affecting other wallets using the module.

The identity of the wallet owner has not been established. Cointelegraph contacted Safe and Gnosis Guild for comment but had not received a response by publication.

Related: DOJ moves to seize $1.2B from Binance hack, disrupts FaceStealer scam

Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery traced funds from the Safe wallet through multiple addresses to Hyperliquid, where five accounts purchased approximately $1 million in XMR1 tokens.

The firm noted similarities with fund movements following Monday’s Lighter incident, including a 160 Ether (ETH) transfer and purchases of XMR1.

However, Bitquery said it found no transfers connecting the two wallet groups and could not establish whether the same actor was involved.

#4959. Nvidia turmoil tests Bitcoin miners’ AI funding plans

Nvidia’s leadership upheaval and Texas permit restrictions sharpen the divide between miners with funded projects and those still seeking capital and approvals.

Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia comes as Bitcoin miners are committing billions of dollars to risky AI infrastructure pivots.

For investors, questions remain around whether large AI contracts can produce cash flows that justify construction costs and support debt service and lead to a sustainable business model. The pivot replaces exposure to Bitcoin (BTC) with construction, financing and customer credit risks. Companies with already-funded projects, usable power and enforceable payment commitments could therefore deliver sharply different returns from peers whose expansion still depends on additional capital and regulatory approvals.

Huang’s departure reaches miners through Nvidia’s overlapping roles as supplier, customer and financier. IREN signed a five-year, $3.4 billion cloud services contract with Nvidia in May, while Nvidia invested $2 billion in CoreWeave in January.

IREN and Applied Digital fell during the Nov. 12 AI selloff following Huang’s departure. For companies seeking equity financing, lower share prices mean issuing more shares to raise the same amount.

JPMorgan credit analyst Erica Spear said “new deals could take longer or require more compensation.” For miners, a slowdown in Nvidia investments, guarantees or capacity purchases could raise financing costs and delay construction. Tighter funding for their cloud-provider tenants could also weaken demand for additional capacity.

Related: Core Scientific to quit Bitcoin mining by year-end as AI business surges

A financing retreat has not been confirmed. Nvidia’s board said it expects operations, customer commitments and its product roadmap to continue uninterrupted.

It is also important to recognize that the AI data center industry is in fact a diverse set of entirely separate business models with their own risk exposures. Leasing powered land, operating colocation facilities, and owning GPUs to sell computing services have different construction requirements, operating responsibilities and equipment replacement exposure.

#4956. Hackers Redirected Bitcoin Miner Rewards via AI Attack, Luxor CEO Says

Hackers Redirected Bitcoin Miner Rewards via AI Attack, Luxor CEO Says

Hackers briefly hijacked computing power from Bitcoin miners using Luxor’s fleet management software, in what the company’s CEO called an AI-enabled attack.

Luxor Technology said Sunday that its internal monitoring flagged an unauthorized redirect of hashrate through Commander, its tool for managing mining machines.

Hashrate is the computing power miners devote to securing Bitcoin and earning rewards. Just over a dozen client accounts were affected, with their machines pointed to a different mining pool for a limited window, effectively sending the value of their work elsewhere.

Luxor said it patched Commander within two hours and began restoring affected machines to their original settings. No data was leaked or taken from its systems, and the issue was isolated to Commander, according to the company.

Luxor Pool and its LuxOS software weren’t affected, the company said, adding that every affected client will be paid in full for the redirected hashrate, as if their machines had mined normally.

Luxor CEO Nick Hansen said the compromise began around 6 p.m. Pacific time Saturday through “a sophisticated AI-enabled vector.” He didn’t detail how the attack worked. “You trust us with your fleet, and we need to be better,” he wrote on X.

Around 6:00p PDT yesterday, a subset of Commander customers were compromised, through a sophisticated AI-enabled vector. We were able to identify and patch quickly so that it didn't continue, then the hard work of reverting started.…

In a follow-up post, Hansen said crypto businesses are now “inundated with AI-enabled attacks,” with abliterated models, or AI models stripped of their safety guardrails, probing systems around the clock for weaknesses.

Luxor has responded by buying its own bare-metal GPUs to run such models defensively. It has also put most new feature work on hold to harden its infrastructure by rotating keys, updating kernels and pinning dependencies. Hansen urged other companies running similar services to do the same.

Bitcoin developers are grappling with the same threat. Bitcoin Core updated its security policy to address AI-driven threats, and an AI “red team” effort has turned up critical vulnerabilities throughout the year.

The incident also follows other attacks on Bitcoin infrastructure. Blockstream’s Liquid Network restored full Bitcoin backing earlier this month, two months after a $320 million exploit.

Luxor said it would soon publish a full post-mortem of the hack.

#4954. 6 Best Travel Dresses of 2026, Tested by a Style Writer and Travel Expert

Our top options are from Uniqlo and lululemon.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

The best travel dresses are the kind you can throw in a carry-on, forget about for hours, and still slip on looking put-together. As a style writer who’s constantly on the move (I checked off eight countries last year alone), I don’t say that lightly. I’ve learned the hard way which pieces wrinkle beyond the help of a hotel room iron, feel restrictive mid-transit, or just don’t pull their styling weight once I land. The ones worth packing work just as well with sneakers as they do with sandals, and make getting dressed in an unfamiliar place easy.

I tested 30-plus styles in real-life conditions, paying close attention to how they pack, wear, and hold up after long days of travel. The best ones strike the sweet spot between comfort and style with breathable fabrics, packable silhouettes, and just enough versatility to earn their spot in my very limited luggage space.

I’ve packed the below dresses for trips to Cancún, Paris, Marrakech, St. Lucia—and plenty of destinations in between—putting them through everything from long-haul flights to full-day itineraries. These are the ones I’ll reach for no matter where I’m headed next.

The Uniqlo Ultra Stretch AIRism Dress rings in at under $40, but the quality feels far more luxe. It’s smooth, polished, and super easy to style in a variety of ways for a single trip—meaning I can wear it multiple times without anyone clocking a repeat outfit.

The fabric is where this dress really shines, IMO. The signature AIRism material is made from 100 percent polyester, making it lightweight, breathable, and quick-drying with a soft, stretchy feel that moves with me. Whether I’m dealing with humid temps or long travel days, it keeps things cool and comfortable without clinging.

It also nails that easy, flattering fit-and-flare shape. It’s more fitted through the bust and subtly flares out toward the legs, creating a flowy drape that I especially love when walking—it just moves beautifully. The midi length hits at about mid-calf, striking that sweet spot between casual and pulled-together, so you can dress it up or down without overthinking it. I wore this dress to Barcelona during a warm September, and the breathable material and loose fit made it a major win.

And if you’re worried about packing a longer dress, don’t be. It packs down incredibly well, and any wrinkles from being in a backpack or suitcase shake out quickly before heading out the door. Plus, it has pockets! A huge win for travel days when you want to easily stash your phone, sunnies, or room key. The only downside: It’s unlined, so the white version is slightly sheer. But that also adds to its airy feel, and there are plenty of other color options if you want more coverage.

The updated lululemon Align Dress is a sporty option that can truly do it all. Designed with yoga in mind, it’s incredibly breathable, stretchy, and sweat-wicking—but doesn’t look overly athletic, thanks to its sleek, sporty-chic silhouette. It transitions seamlessly from a morning flow to a full day of sightseeing, making it one of those rare pieces I always throw into my suitcase.

The updated version improves on the original Align Dress with a nylon base and even more elastane, giving it more stretch and wrinkle resistance—yes, even after being packed down in compression cubes. Just like the brand’s famed Align leggings, this fabric feels ultra-smooth and lightweight.

Fit-wise, it features an A-line silhouette, meaning it's more fitted through the torso and gradually flares out toward the hem for a flattering drape. The mini length hits at about mid-thigh, keeping things cool and unfussy. From a packing and styling perspective, it’s a no-brainer. The shorter length and featherlight fabric make it easy to toss into your suitcase and unpack with minimal wrinkles. The only real downside is the price—it’s one of the most expensive picks on this list—but considering the quality, performance fabric, and versatility, it’s worth the investment (watch out, as it’s often on sale).

Stylish, short-sleeve dresses under $100 can be surprisingly hard to find. That’s why the Free People Blaine Midi Dress is one of my new faves. The overall vibe leans laid-back with that signature Free People look—think relaxed and boho but still put together.

Made from 100% cotton, the fabric is soft, breathable, and especially comfortable in heat and humidity. What I really love, though, is the subtly textured, crinkled finish paired with dramatic pleating, which keeps wrinkles at bay.

This long-sleeve dress gives just the right amount of coverage on the arms but excels at breathability. That makes it perfect for everything from long-haul flights or bus rides to cooler evenings. It feels light and airy without sacrificing style, with an easy silhouette that still looks thoughtfully put together.

The fabric is a standout: a soft, gauzy 100% organic cotton that feels breathable and gentle against the skin. Like the Free People dress, it has a naturally textured, crinkled finish, so it doesn’t show wrinkles, even after being packed. Instead of pleating, it features a flouncy, tiered skirt with horizontal seaming, which adds movement and a bit of playful volume.

Fit-wise, it leans relaxed and slightly oversized, so sizing down is a smart move if you want a more tailored look. Meet the perfect mini dress. I own it in black, and it always looks incredibly chic—whether I’m dressing it up with heels for a city dinner or keeping it casual with sandals for daytime plans. The fabric plays a big role in that versatility. It has a classic, body-skimming silhouette that gently follows your shape without feeling tight or restrictive. The mini length hits at about mid-thigh, while the boat neckline adds a classy feel that instantly upgrades the overall look. It’s simple, but in that very polished, well-designed way.

It checks all the boxes for travel. The Bond Dress packs down easily, comes out looking polished, and can be styled in multiple ways depending on your itinerary. If there's a downside, it's that the streamlined fit doesn't leave much room for built-in functionality like shorts or roomy pockets, but the trade-off is a sleek, goes-with-anything mini you’ll reach for again and again.

The Dylan Mini Dress earns its spot as the most stylish pick thanks to its ultra-flattering shape and the prettiest range of colors and patterns. It has that slightly romantic feel that instantly dresses up your outfit, whether you’re heading to dinner or just wandering a new city. I always get compliments when I wear this dress (it was a major hit during my trip to Mallorca)—and it looks just as good in photos as it does in person.

The fit is where it really stands out. It has a flattering scoop neckline trimmed with delicate lace, plus a fitted bodice that dips slightly at the waist to help elongate your torso. From there, it flows into a long, airy skirt that moves beautifully as you walk. Adjustable straps let you customize the fit, and the built-in bra with removable pads adds support without the need for extra layers—always a win when packing light.

In terms of length, it hits a few inches above the ankles for that easy, breezy feel, and it comes in petite, regular, and tall options so you can find your ideal fit. Since traveling involves lots of packing, travel expert Addie Bell says to look for wrinkle-resistant materials like spandex, nylon, or polyester. If you’re only traveling with a carry-on or trying to maximize storage, stick to neutral tones like black, navy, white, and beige, which are versatile and easy to mix and match with other wardrobe pieces. "Subtle patterns can also help hide wrinkles and stains, making the dress more travel-friendly," says Bell. But bright colors can add a fun, vibrant touch. "I always recommend sticking within a similar color palette to ensure they match other items you’re bringing.”

#4953. The 7 Best Body Groomers for Men in 2026, Tested by Grooming Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Trimmers and shavers for everywhere below the neck.

LIKE EVERYTHING ELSE, body grooming trends come and go. Just look at the wild, hairy 1970s or the Ken doll slick early aughts if you don’t believe me. Right now, we are living in what I would argue is the golden age of body hair. As in, you can do whatever you want with it. You can trim! You can wax! You can let it grow… and grow… and grow!

But the reality is that most men (at least 62 percent) do something to their body hair. This isn’t to say that you’re required to manscape, but whether you already do or you’re about to give it a try for the first time, the most important thing in any manscaping journey is the tool you use.

Anyone who has shaved even once knows that the risk of cutting and nicking skin is very real, especially when you get down to very sensitive or hard-to-reach areas. Trimming, whether it's using hair clippers or electric razors, has its own set of headaches in the form of pulling hairs and not having enough protection between the blade and your skin.

That’s where the best body groomers come in—they’re specifically designed to be gentle on sensitive areas (like your twig and berries) and make the grooming experience way more pleasant. And before you ask why you need another tool for this job, consider this: Using the same razor or trimmer on your body as you do on your face can lead to bacterial cross-contamination. Do you really want jock itch on your chin?

These days, body and pubic trimmers are technologically advanced to help make the job way easier. We’re talking long-lasting charges, waterproof casings, multiple guards, special blades, and more. So whatever hair you’re hoping to tackle, and no matter how much of it you have, the best body groomers will get the job done quickly and comfortably.

Throughout our testing of over 50 body groomers, we found that Panasonic's GK80 is the best in class. There’s a lot to love about this groomer. The unique V-shaped blade and ergonomic design allow you to trim even the hardest-to-reach crevices with ease, and the innovative length guard oscillates between 12 different lengths with the turn of a dial, so you never have to take it off while switching lengths. It delivers one of the most customizable and easiest experiences you could hope for in a body trimmer.

What Else to Consider: The innovative design of this groomer is what sets it apart, but it still takes a bit of a learning curve to figure out the best way to use it on your body. It doesn’t follow the traditional push vs. pull methods that most trimmers do. Because of the V-shaped blade, it’s able to cut in both directions, which does make it easier, but if you’re switching from using a more traditional groomer, it can feel weird at first. The adjustable trimmer head is effective, but also bulky and may take some practice getting used to.

It’s convenient to avoid completely switching combs in the middle of a trimming session, but it can also make the trimmer feel a little top-heavy, and some of our testers found it reduces the effectiveness of the blades. The rinse-to-clean capability is great, but we’d advise using it dry instead of wet (that goes for pretty much all of these trimmers, to be honest).

Why We Chose It: For sheer ease of use, the Panasonic Body Groomer GK80 cannot be beat. The innovative design, multi-directional cutting capability, adjustable dial length comb, and V-shaped head all combine to make this easily the most intuitive and efficient body groomer available. Sure, it’s not perfect—it’s slightly better at shaving than trimming, for instance—but its pros exceed its cons by a landslide.

We found in our testing that using it dry is more effective, but it’s just as comfortable shaving your more sensitive groin areas as it is for the chest, arms, and shoulders. And while it is on the expensive side, if you groom or trim your body hair regularly, it’s a solid investment.

Long-Term Testing Notes: We’ve been using this device for over two years, and the effectiveness of the Body Groomer GK80 has not waned. What we have noticed, however, is that it's better for shaving than trimming. Not that it does a bad job; it’s just that the shaving capability is better than the other trimmers in our arsenal (save for perhaps the Philips Norelco OneBlade), while the trimming capabilities with the adjustable comb are comparable to some others. Still, it remains our go-to trimmer because of how comfortable it is to hold and how nimble it is at cutting hair in hard-to-reach places, thanks to the wand design.Read More: Panasonic GK80 Review

Whether you want to mow the lawn completely or just give it a little trim, this groomer does it all. This new, more advanced version is completely waterproof, so you can use it in the shower (Cleanup? Done). Plus, it has a wireless dock that makes charging a breeze. With multiple-length combs and ceramic blades that are gentle on even your most sensitive areas, this is one of the most effective body groomers out there.

What Else to Consider: This is a classic push-style trimmer, which means you push it toward you (usually against the grain) to cut the hair. This is not a bad thing, just good to know going into the purchase, in case you are used to a pull-style trimmer. The single adjustable length comb only has a couple of length capabilities, so this trimmer isn’t optimized for a variety of body hair options—it’s really designed to shave down to the skin or leave just a little bit of stubble.

You’re not going to do a bunch of contouring or style changes with this. And while it’s designed specifically for the tender groin area, many users have noted that it can still nick skin pretty easily if you’re not extra careful. The intuitive features, like the LED spotlight to help you see where you are trimming and the new wireless charging dock, are all welcome.

Why We Chose It: If you’re a consistent trimmer of your undercarriage, the Manscaper 5.0 is one of the best tools out there to get the job done effectively. It delivers a clean-shaven look with ease anywhere you want it, and when compared to a traditional razor, it is way more comfortable and less risky, even with the fact that it can still nick skin.

We also love the additional features that many of the other groomers on this list don’t have, like a wireless charging dock and LED spotlight (it may seem gimmicky at first, but trust us, it helps). It’s an intuitively designed device that delivers what it promises and then some. As long as you’re looking for a close shave, it’s a good bet.

Long-Term Testing Notes: Months after first testing the Manscaper 5.0, we still go back to it for specific areas of our bodies, namely the undercarriage. Once you get the hang of the pull method, it shaves easily and quickly. A word of advice, though: Do not try to go fast or cut corners. Make sure you give yourself adequate time to use it slowly, or the risk of nicks and cuts increases exponentially.

Read More: Manscaped The Lawn Mower 5.0 Review

This hybrid electric trimmer and shaver is super gentle on your skin yet extremely effective at removing body hair to your desired length. Use the guards for trimming if you like to leave a little length, or take them off for a super close shave that never leaves any cuts or scratches.

What Else To Consider: If you're new to full-body manscaping, especially around the nether regions, and are nervous about nicking the family jewels, this is the perfect tool for you. More than any other device on this list, the OneBlade rarely—if ever—cuts or pulls hair. Now, a major side effect of this is that it can only shave to just above completely bald. So if you're looking to go entirely bare, it might be worth investing elsewhere.

Why We Chose It: Of course, the OneBlade still gives an incredibly close shave, even if it doesn't leave skin 100 percent bald. We tend to value ease of use, reliability, and safety over a smooth shave when it comes to body grooming, which is why we constantly find ourselves reaching back for the OneBlade over and over.

Long-Term Testing Notes: Simply put, the Philips Norelco OneBlade continues to be a staple in our grooming arsenal. From its innovative design to its ergonomic head, this device is one of the most versatile devices we've tested. Not to mention, its waterproof capabilities, battery life, and shave power have not waned at all over time.

Read More: Philips Norelco OneBlade Review

This kit comes with everything you need for head-to-toe grooming. It can also be used in the shower if you prefer a wet shave. It includes eight combs covering 40 precision lengths (!!), a detail trimmer, and ear and nose trimmer attachments.

What Else to Consider: The only difference between this version of the Series 7 and the original meant to be used on your face is that it comes with different guards that can leave hair longer and are designed specifically for the body. Other than that, the functionality and design are the same. Additionally, while the more recent Series 9 is a better beard trimmer, we find that the Series 7 handles body hair with a bit more ease.

In both, there’s a specific skin safeguard designed for below-the-belt grooming to protect your more sensitive skin from the razor, but the Series 9 is slightly gentler, which can struggle from time to time with body hair. You can still use the Series 7 on your face, of course, but you should use a different blade. Luckily, the one comes with a second blade to easily switch back and forth by just popping them off. Pro tip: Keep them in different cases or label them so you don’t get the blades mixed up.

Why We Chose It: Here at Men’s Health, we are huge fans of the Braun Series 7 simply because it can’t be matched in its functionality, portability, and versatility. Keep in mind that it’s best suited for areas you want to shave or leave a slight stubble. If your goal is an easy, quick, and efficient shave anywhere on your body, this is the tool for you.

Long-Term Testing Notes: The Braun Series 7 is a game-changer in terms of shaving. We use it anywhere on our bodies that we want a clean, close shave, like our shoulders, back, and face (of course, using different blades).

We don’t tend to use it to trim, as the length combs only really offer shorter options, and without a carrying case, the combs tend to get lost at the bottom of our bathroom drawers. It is handy for any sort of tapering or contouring body hair because it’s easy to handle.

Read More: Braun All-in-One Series 7 Trimmer Review

If you’re into streamlining, this all-in-one trimmer does everything: your hair, your beard, and your body (just make sure to clean it before switching locations—it’s fully washable). The self-sharpening blades keep the cutting power strong, and the plethora of guards and attachments make trimming or cutting any hair on your body easy. And with five hours of cordless run time, you can easily go from head to toe without recharging.

What Else to Consider: Using a clipper for everything is convenient, but it requires some adjusting of your technique depending on where you use it. This multipurpose groomer is optimized for cutting the hair on your head, so it’s powerful—more powerful than some of the other dedicated body groomers on this list.

That means proceed with caution when taking it downstairs to more sensitive areas. Use it with a guard to get the hang of it and avoid nicks and cuts on your tender bits in the process. You’ll also want to thoroughly clean it before using it on your head or beard to avoid cross-contamination.

Why We Chose It: As far as multipurpose groomers go, the Philips Norelco Multigroomer is top-of-the-line. We love that it’s hefty and durable and feels more like a traditional hair clipper than anything else. Also, we found that it’s incredibly powerful and can cut through even thick, coarse hair with ease.

You also can’t beat the options you get with 18 different attachments. It’s able to do any cutting, trimming, or detailing you could possibly want. It truly is an all-in-one tool ready to attack whatever you throw at it.

Long-Term Testing Notes: Even after the testing phase, the Philips Norelco Multigroomer continues to be one of our go-to tools for trimming and cutting hair. But we find ourselves reaching for it more as a hair clipper and beard trimmer than a full-on body groomer.

We tend to use it more on less-sensitive areas like our chests. And when it comes time to trim below the belt, we reach for something a little more gentle. That said, it’s still well worth the investment if you don’t want to clutter your bathroom with multiple tools.

Read More: Philips Norelco Multigroomer All-in-One Review

Don't worry if you're not flexible: This handy tool lets you reach all areas of your back by yourself. An added Power Burst button shaves through extra-thick and coarse hair.

What Else to Consider: Shaving your back is hard to achieve on your own with a traditional body groomer—it’s usually a two-person job. The long, angled arm of this shaver is specifically designed to allow you to fully shave your back without help.

There are two heads, but they are both shavers—one is just wider than the other to cover more surface area. There aren’t any length attachments here because of the assumption that most guys want to completely shave their backs, and that’s probably true.

Like with any trimmer, there is a slight learning curve to using it, but especially this one, as it still takes some dexterity to understand where you are shaving and to see your progress in the mirror. It’s also not designed to shave or trim other parts of your body because of the bulky, angled arm. It’s not for everyone, but if you regularly shave your back (or have someone else do it for you), it could be worth the investment.

Why We Chose It: We’ll say it again, we are always fans of using the best tool for whatever job you’re doing. Back shaving is incredibly tough to do on your own, so anything that helps make that process easier is great in our book. It’s relatively simple to use and isn’t bogged down with extra functions to confuse the process. Once you get the hang of it, it’s an important tool in your body grooming arsenal if your back is a focal point for you.

Long-Term Testing Notes: Over a year of using this tool, its battery life still holds up for hours. That being said, we have had to replace the foil (totally expected once you pass the year mark). But once the blades started to dull, we found them to be more prone to hair pulling.

Not only do the stainless steel blades cut through even the coarsest hair, but the rounded, wraparound guards protect your junk from nicks and cuts. The integrated dial allows a whopping 39 (!) different cutting lengths for a truly customized experience. Plus, it’s completely waterproof and has a 100-minute run time on a single charge.

What Else to Consider: If you’re a fan of trimming in the shower, this option is one of the best for wet use. We found that it's completely waterproof, which makes shower shaving a breeze, not to mention cleanup. Just keep in mind that, in general, wet trimming is slightly more difficult than dry trimming—but of course, you can’t beat that cleanup.

The wraparound guard design makes it less harrowing to trim your sensitive areas, but it won’t give you the closest shave. For that, you’ll have to take it off, which is still comfortable, but more prone to nicks and cuts. And if you’re a frequent traveler who likes to trim on the go, the travel lock is important since it doesn’t come with a case.

Why We Chose It: For a more inexpensive trimmer, this one still has all the features you want, like a quick charge option, wet/dry functionality, and a variety of lengths. Not to mention, some that you didn’t know you wanted, but once you try, you’ll love, like the rotary dial to adjust trimming length easily without needing to switch combs.

Overall, this groomer is reliable and versatile, and while the blades are not quite as sharp as more premium models, it still gets the job done when you need it to.

Long-Term Testing Notes: After a year of use, the Wahl Manscaper is still able to handle whatever hair we throw at it without a struggle. That being said, while it remains usable in water, we have found that 100-minute battery life to be more like 90 minutes—though that's still longer than most other options available.

In general, body hair is thicker than facial hair, so you'll need devices that have more power than your typical electric razor. That said, we suggest looking for a tool with an extensive battery life, so you'll spend less time charging and more time shaving. In our experience, that's something with at least 40 minutes or more of runtime. The groomers we've selected as the best have battery lives that extend from 40 minutes to six hours.

Manscaping during or directly after showering can make the whole process much more seamless, with less risk of nicks or pulling. For this, you'll want to check out options that are water-resistant to ensure you can use them while you take a shower or right after you hop out. This will also assist in the cleaning process, as you can simply run the tool under water and leave everything out until it dries.

Every trimmer on this list is electric, which means they have one of two blade types: rotary or foil. In general, the biggest difference between the two is that rotary blades cut hair in a circular motion while foil blades cut in one direction, essentially up and down or side to side. Foils also typically cut closer, but rotary blades are more adept at maneuvering the contours of the body. That being said, rotary blades are better at attacking thicker or coarser hair, while foils are often more gentle on sensitive skin. So it really comes down to what you value more.

When it comes to electric grooming devices, chargers have come a long way from their battery-powered origins (although there are still plenty of these options around for those who prefer them). The two main alternatives to batteries are a cord or plug directly connecting the tool to an outlet and a stand that charges the groomer while it's mounted. Neither is necessarily better than the other (including the battery-powered); it mostly comes down to personal preference.

That being said, depending on your bathroom setup, you may want to zero in on certain options. For those with limited counter or storage space, you’ll probably want to opt for a plug that you can charge when needed and then store when not in use. But if you have the counter space, a charging mount can be super convenient and help keep your device sufficiently charged at all times.

Body hair can differ significantly in prevalence, thickness, and sensitivity from one area to another. With this in mind, many devices will include multiple blades meant specifically for various areas of the body. This also helps from a hygiene standpoint, as you wouldn’t want to reuse the same blade for every crevice of the body to avoid cross-contamination between different zones.

Just as different parts of your body require different blades, you probably won’t want every area to maintain the same length of hair. For example, you may want your back to be as bald as possible, but probably not your chest (unless you’re a competitive swimmer or bodybuilder). For this, varying attachments that offer different desired lengths can be super helpful, especially if you’re someone who does widespread body grooming.

If you’re anything like us, you value organization when it comes to your grooming arsenal. It makes sense; the more tools and products you have, the more space they’ll take up, and the more likely you are to lose track of attachments, cords, and anything else that’s not directly connected to your device. This is where a case can really be crucial to help hold all of your body groomer’s attachments and gadgets in one convenient place.

For the past three years, Men's Health's grooming editors and writers have done extensive research and testing for body groomers. Throughout this time, we have tested over 50 body groomers (both wet and dry) for extended periods of time, evaluating all the picks on effectiveness, safety, comfort, ease of use, reliability, battery life, and value. From there, we then trimmed (get it?) the list down to the seven best body groomers for men that are worth your money.

My passport book is nearly out of blank pages, and I’m starting to worry that my next trip will require an emergency upgrade to make it through customs. But as a frequent flyer and style writer, one thing I don’t stress over is what to wear to the airport. Between maxing out my PTO and logging plenty of miles for work (including tons of in-transit testing for WH Travel Awards), I’ve mastered the art of the airport fit. And while I firmly believe that wearing jeans on a plane should land you on the no-fly list, I’m all about wearing something comfortable without looking like I’m wearing pajamas at the terminal.

That’s where the right pair of travel pants comes in clutch, hitting that happy medium between polished and comfortable. I’m talking about pants you can sit in for hours, sprint through a terminal in, and still wear straight to dinner without a second thought. Over time (and many, many flights), I’ve narrowed down the pairs that truly deliver: versatile, low-maintenance styles that work just as well in your suitcase as they do on your body, from takeoff to touchdown.

The Vuori Halo Essential Wideleg pant has been at the top of my drawer since I got my first pair nearly a year ago. I’m obsessed with the super-soft and smooth polyester and elastane blend. It feels nearly pajama-like while looking way more polished than your average sweatpant (especially if you opt for a darker color like black or navy).

I often reach for this pant when getting dressed for the airport because I know I’ll be comfortable on the plane and that I’ll wear it at least once during my trip. The wide-leg silhouette skims the body in a really flattering way without looking baggy or oversized. It looks great paired with Vuori’s matching zip-up and my fave Dr. Scholl’s Time Off Sneaker for long-haul flights, but it just as easily dresses up with a cute sandal and a form-fitting tank or tee.

Oh, and the pant never wrinkles. It feels soft and cotton-like but since it's made from a buttery synthetic blend, it always looks sleek—more quiet luxury than airport chaos. The material isn’t too thick either, so I don’t find myself overheating while wearing it, even when I land in a sunny destination. I wore this pant while traveling to Mexico recently and felt totally comfortable from takeoff in New York until I arrived at the hotel.

If you’re looking for an under-$50 find that holds its own against pricier pairs, the Old Navy Linen-Blend Ankle Pant is it. Made from a 55% linen blend, it delivers the airy look and feel you want from linen—without the steep price tag most comparable styles carry.

Comfort-wise, it’s exactly what I want for a travel day: lightweight, breathable, and stylish. The secret is in the fabric. This pant blends linen with rayon, a semi-synthetic fiber derived from natural sources like wood pulp that’s known for being soft, smooth, and less prone to creasing than 100% linen. The result is breezy but cozy fabric that doesn’t feel remotely scratchy or itchy. I also love the clean, straight-leg silhouette and high waist that makes me feel put-together with next to zero effort.

I will say, this is one of those pairs I prefer to wear on the plane rather than pack, since it picks up a few more wrinkles when folded in a suitcase (it is still linen, after all). But once I put it on, the fabric bounces back nicely—and I end up reaching for it constantly throughout my trip. The pant is endlessly versatile: I’ll throw it on with flat sandals and a white tee for daytime exploring, then swap in a blouse and heels for dinner without missing a beat.

If you didn’t know better, you might mistake the lululemon Daydrift High-Rise Wide-Leg Trouser for a lounge pant—but one mirror check and it’s giving Succession-coded energy. It’s my go-to for when I need to land and immediately be “on,” whether that’s heading to a meeting or traveling with colleagues.

Made primarily from nylon and elastane, this pant is breathable, sweat-wicking, and cool to the touch—exactly what I want for a long day on the go. It has a smooth, tailored look that resists wrinkling, making it especially suitcase-friendly. It also features a stretch waistband with an internal drawstring, which makes a big difference when I’m sitting for hours or dealing with the general unpredictability of travel days.

I’ll wear it with my go-to Uniqlo Crew Neck T-Shirt and sneakers for a more casual, on-the-move look, but it just as easily leans corporate with a button-down or blazer. Swap in a silky top and heels and it even holds its own for evening plans. It’s that comfort and versatility that make it such a staple in my everyday and travel wardrobe.

If you want something that feels barely there for a warm-weather vacation, the FP Movement Champ Is Here Pant is my top rec. Made from 100% nylon, it’s airy and flowy and allows for total free range of movement—perfect for long travel days or more active itineraries. And thanks to the barrel-leg silhouette (meaning it’s a bit wider at the knee area) and the subtle contrast piping, it still feels on-trend.

Its nylon construction is naturally lightweight, quick-drying, and impressively durable, which is great if your trip involves anything beyond just walking through airports and lounging around. The water-resistant finish and a reinforced woven design help resist tearing and ripping, so it holds up whether you’re caught in a drizzle, heading out on a hike, or just putting it through its paces. But it still feels soft and breathable—not stiff or overly technical.

“I’m a big fan of track pants, and the second I bought this pair, I had travel in mind,” says associate editor Olivia Luppino. “The open, barrel-leg fit makes it super comfortable and yet fashionable to wear on a plane—and I’ve also worn it on a hike, as a beach cover-up, and even dressed it up for dinner.” I’ve found the same—it looks great with sneakers and a tank for daytime, or a fitted top and sandals for nighttime. The only small caveat is the rise: it does sit quite high, which can feel like a lot if you have a shorter torso (I sometimes fold the waistband down for a more comfortable fit).

If you’ve ever tried to juggle your phone, passport, lip balm, and boarding pass while sprinting through a terminal, you get the value of a pocketed pair of pants. The Athleta Skyline High Rise Barrel Leg Pant is my fave in the category. The deep, secure pockets make a huge difference when I’m on the go and don’t want to constantly dig through my bag like I’m Mary Poppins.

Made from polyester, cotton, and spandex, it has a structured, almost denim-like feel—but with way more stretch. The pant has a polished, slightly tailored look, but with the kind of softness and flexibility that makes long flights and all-day wear far more comfortable. The breathable fabric allows for airflow and quick-drying properties that come in handy if you’re on the move (or caught in less-than-ideal weather). There’s even UPF 40+ protection for extra coverage on sunny days. I sort of think of it as an upgraded cargo pant— functional, but not in a “I just came from REI” kind of way.

The barrel-leg silhouette adds a slightly relaxed shape that still feels put-together, and the material isn’t too bulky. I love that this pant works for air travel, city exploring, light hikes, and casual dinners. The only downside? The slightly more structured fabric means they’re not quite as soft or drapey as some of the other pairs on this list—but I still find the fit super flattering.

I usually don’t wear sweatpants during travel because they read way too casual compared to a jogger or trousers. But for longer flights, I sometimes make an exception—and this is the pair I’ll reach for. The straight-leg silhouette feels a bit more put-together than most other sweatpants, but it’s still super soft and lightweight. This sweatpant looks great with almost any casual fit, but our style team loves wearing it with Alo’s color-coordinating jackets and hoodies for a chic, monochrome vibe.

It’s made with a French terry cloth (a cotton blend that’s smooth on the outside) and stylist Alexandra Juric says this makes for a soft, breathable fleece lining. It has a slightly oversized look, but if you want a more snug fit, you can size down. However, I’m into the oversized look and love that this pair doesn’t fit too tightly on the lower belly, since other popular sweatpants I’ve tested can emphasize that area too much. Style contributor Lily Wohlner also prefers it a bit bigger, as she can always roll down the waistband for a more snug fit around the hips.

“The only downside to these sweats is the length; the pants go well past my ankle, making them hard to wear outside,” says Juric. But, sizing down, rolling the waistband, or wearing a platform sneaker would likely solve that problem.

The Vince Bias Cut High Waist Pant is easily the most stylish pair of travel pants in my rotation. It has a liquid-like drape that instantly makes any outfit feel more luxe and the fit is incredibly flattering. I wore it nonstop on my last trip to Spain—on the plane, out to dinner, even just wandering during the day—and it somehow always looked chic with minimal effort.

It’s made from a blend of acetate (a semi-synthetic fiber derived from wood pulp—known for a silky feel and subtle sheen) and polyester, which gives this pant that drapey fit. The bias cut, which refers to cutting the fabric diagonally across the grain, allows the material to skim the body rather than cling to it, creating a fluid effect that I find super flattering. It also gives the pant a natural stretch and tons of movement, so it doesn’t feel restrictive. Add in the high waist and the range of chic neutrals it comes in and you have a truly classic-looking pant.

During my last trip, I styled this pant with a simple tank and sandals during the day, then swapped in a blouse and heels at night. It packs relatively well, too, thanks to that fluid fabric—and because it’s so lightweight, it doesn’t take up much space in a carry-on. The only downside is the care: it’s hand wash, line dry, which isn’t always the most convenient if you need to freshen up mid-trip.

If comfort is your top priority, the Skims Cotton Jersey Foldover Pant is the softest pair in the lineup. This is the kind of pant I put on for a flight and immediately feel better—like I’m wearing my favorite pajamas but still look pulled together enough to step off the plane without a full outfit change. It’s an ideal pant for long-haul days, early morning departures, or anytime you just want to feel cozy without fully leaning into sleepwear or baggy silhouettes.

It’s made from a jersey blend (mostly cotton with a touch of elastane), which is what gives it that ultra-soft, slightly stretchy feel. Cotton keeps things breathable and gentle against the skin, while elastane adds just enough give for when you’re sitting, walking, or curled up in a window seat. The foldover waistband is a standout feature—it lets you customize the rise depending on your preference, whether you want a more low-slung, relaxed fit or a bit more coverage. The fabric has that smooth, second-skin quality that moves with you, making it especially great for travel days when comfort is non-negotiable.

That said, it’s more versatile than you might expect. I’ll wear it with a simple tank and sneakers for an easy airport look, but it also works with a structured jacket to feel a bit more put-together. It also packs down to almost nothing, making it a great backup option in your carry-on. The one trade-off is that it does lean more casual—so while it’s perfect for the plane and low-key plans, it’s not quite as polished as some of the other options here.

Look for pants made with materials that are:

Packing smarter starts with choosing capsule wardrobe essentials that pull double (or triple) duty—think a crisp button-down that you can wear over a tank or tucked into trousers, a lightweight knit that works on the plane and at dinner, or a simple slip dress that doubles as a beach coverup and dinner outfit. Travel pants should follow that same philosophy: versatile enough to style casually with sneakers and a tee, but polished enough to pair with a blouse or blazer. Building multiple outfits around one reliable piece avoids overpacking and makes dressing while on vacation way easier.

Since studying abroad in 2019, I’ve been traveling nonstop. #4950. How Dwight Howard Built His ‘Superman’ Physique

The NBA center talks training, injuries, and discipline.

MORE THAN OTHER pro athletes, NBA players tend to enter their professional careers as skinny kids, still developing out of high school. To a degree, that’s exactly what happened with Dwight Howard, the first pick of the 2004 NBA draft. “My first year in the league, I got kind of pushed around,” Howard said on MH’s Strong Talk. “I didn’t like it.” Howard spent that offseason “eating weights” and became on the most muscular (and dominant) players ever. He earned the nickname “Superman” and went on to a Hall of Fame career. For almost two decades, Howard played for multiple teams and won an NBA championship with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020.

Howard’s superhero physique came from more than shooting hoops. The center began building a disciplined training regimen as a high schooler, waking up at 4 a.m. to run track and hit the weight room.

“I told my dad at 10 I wanted to go to the NBA, and he said, ‘Well, you got to learn how to sacrifice now. You know your time and your effort. You have to learn how to be disciplined,’” Howard says in the latest Strong Talk episode.

Howard took his dad’s words to heart, already having the foresight that establishing a routine now would be easier than breaking bad training habits upon entering the NBA. His training over the years has evolved into different fitness challenges: from training in high-altitude terrains in Aspen to taking on Pilates and yoga.

Speaking with MH fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. and exercise physiologist and strength coach Dr. Pat Davidson, Howard goes into detail about the strength exercises he did to stay fit during the season, what he’s learned from trying to play through injuries, and the upcoming launch of the Rize Above with Dwight app next month that will offer fitness guidance to individuals of any age starting a fitness journey.

#4948. Coinbase and Broadridge propose standard for tokenized stock disclosures

The proposed standard aims to connect tokenized stockholders with corporate disclosures and voting materials across digital wallets, but would not create shareholder rights.

Coinbase and Broadridge proposed a technical standard Monday that would let digital wallets find and display shareholder notices linked to tokenized stocks.

The jointly developed Onchain Rights Standard would give issuers, custodians and wallet providers a shared format for communications about dividends, shareholder meetings and other corporate actions. Broadridge separately announced a supporting data service, known as an oracle, intended to help participating firms document the distribution of those notices.

The proposal’s technical documentation describes an onchain announcement that links a token to a standardized corporate document. A dividend notice, for example, could specify the date, payment terms and any choices available to holders. Compatible wallets could then display notices from different issuers using the same format, reducing the need for multiple other integrations.

“The proposed standard is a communications framework; it does not itself create shareholder rights,” Mark Nichols, Broadridge’s co-president of digital assets, told Cointelegraph.

Nichols said implementation would depend on the underlying structure of each tokenized stock, including whether holders have direct shareholder rights.

The companies said they submitted the proposal for review as an Ethereum Improvement Proposal. They did not name additional adopters of the standard or give an implementation timetable.

Broadridge launched its onchain shareholder governance platform in April, naming Galaxy as an intended user for its May shareholder meeting. The platform integrates Broadridge’s ProxyVote system with digital wallets, allowing investors to receive shareholder materials, confirm holdings and submit votes, with voting records maintained on an Avalanche-based blockchain.

#4947. Bitcoin's $2 Billion Liquidation Weekend Leaves Traders Watching $60,000

Bitcoin's $2 Billion Liquidation Weekend Leaves Traders Watching $60,000

Bitcoin fell to around $62,100 on Sunday as roughly $2 billion in crypto derivatives positions were forcibly closed, mostly bets that prices would rise. The weekend slide sent the cryptocurrency to its lowest level since July 14, adding another ugly chapter to six consecutive weeks of losses.

Bitcoin had recovered to around $64,300 early Monday. But the options market is showing why traders aren't necessarily treating that bounce as an all-clear.

Liquidations happen when an exchange closes a trader's position because the money posted to support a borrowed bet is no longer enough to cover its losses. CoinGlass figures from Saturday showed $1.9 billion liquidated in one 24-hour period, about $1.8 billion of it bullish positions across cryptocurrencies, not just Bitcoin.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had already been losing investors before the weekend. Data from Decrypt’s ETF tracker show $185.4 million in net outflows on Friday, extending their losing streak to seven trading sessions and bringing withdrawals since November 5 to approximately $1.91 billion.

BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $143.5 million of Friday's withdrawals, while Fidelity's FBTC lost $41.9 million. The funds' earlier weakness had helped explain the broader exodus, although ETF flow totals measure fund creations and redemptions rather than every trade between investors.

Those numbers also come with a timing distinction: U.S. ETFs do not trade over the weekend, while Bitcoin trades around the clock. Friday's outflows show weakened demand before the crash, not that ETF shareholders were redeeming shares during Sunday's plunge.

Bitcoin's technical indicators suggest the selling may be overstretched, but that doesn't necessarily mean the worst is over.

The daily Relative Strength Index sat near 24 in oversold territory on the daily charts. Meanwhile, the Average Directional Index stood above 33, indicating a strong prevailing trend, with bearish directional pressure still dominating. The weekly RSI, near 38, pointed to a weak longer-term picture, although it had not reached oversold territory.

The cryptocurrency bounced after approaching support around $62,000. A recovery would face potential resistance near $66,500 to $67,200, followed by another obstacle around $69,300, based on the chart's Fibonacci levels that measure support and resistance marks.

A decisive break below $62,000, meanwhile, would put the psychologically important $60,000 level back in focus—precisely where options traders have accumulated significant downside exposure.

Bitcoin's next test will be whether fresh U.S. ETF flow data show more withdrawals for Monday and whether traders keep paying for downside protection. The heavily watched November 27 options expiration is still ahead, with $50,000 puts among the contracts drawing the most recent trading activity.
