When it comes to comfortable athleisure wear that you can sport almost every day, Lululemon churns out the best of the best. Take the brand's relaxed-fitting style hoodie, which doesn't feel too loose or baggy. We found there's plenty of room in the chest and at the waist, meaning you can easily layer long-sleeve T-shirts and still receive a great deal of breathability. Plus, the cotton-blend fabric has a hint of stretch, so it's perfect for guys with broader shoulders and bigger biceps.

Our style editors raved about how breathable the fabric is, making it a top option for all-day wear, from their workout class to the beer hall. Thanks to the brushed interior, you get that next-to-skin warmth that keeps you feeling toasty when the temps dip. Despite its steep price point, this fleece pullover can handle several washes and multiple seasons. We've worn it through the fall and into the spring—pairing it with chinos, jeans, and sweats.

And if you don't feel like carrying your backpack, the Steady State Hoodie comes with a wide kangaroo pouch, so there's a place to store your phone, wallet, beanie—or warm your hands.

Abercrombie’s hoodie is my go-to for travel days when all I care about is being comfortable on my flights. The fit runs a little oversized, but it doesn’t make you look like you’re wearing a puffy trash bag. You get extra room in the body and waist with the option to layer anything that’s slim-fitting or slightly bulky. If you like a closer fit, just size down.

I’ve had mine for a couple of years now, and the cotton-polyester fabric still feels as soft as the day I unboxed it. I’ve put it through countless washes, coffee spills, and lazy weekends, and yet the color and shape haven’t budged. I’ve also wore it during a chilly fall photoshoot and was impressed by how it held up against the wind better than half of the performance hoodies we tested.

Style-wise, it’s one of those hoodies that just works with anything—sweatpants, jeans, joggers, or even chino pants when you’re dressing up for casual Fridays. The washed finish gives it a vintage, lived-in vibe that looks polished, not sloppy. And while it skips the drawstring, I’ve never once wished it had one—the hood stays put even when the wind kicks up. The front pouch pocket is spacious enough to keep your hands warm on cold morning errand runs. Plus, this hoodie comes in an insane amount of colors to choose from.

When it comes to hoodies, Champion wrote the playbook. More than a decade after my college years, the brand’s still cranking out affordable sweats like this one that feel anything but cheap. The cotton-polyester blend is thick, soft, and surprisingly resilient, while the patented reverse weave technique (a unique manufacturing process) boosts its lifespan and reduces shrinking, wash after wash. After six washing cycles, the fabric held up nicely without becoming dingy or pilling. Compared to other hoodies that we've tested, this might be the heaviest option on the list, meaning you get all the cozy vibes without feeling weighed down.

The loose cut leaves room to layer over basics, and the hoodie stretches just enough for reaching, bending, or grabbing a coffee on the go. While it might be too warm for a cool summer night, it’s perfect for fall walks, weekend errands, or casual hangouts. Either way, it keeps you toasty during shoulder season without needing a fleece jacket. We also love how effortlessly it pairs with jeans, sweats, or relaxed trousers—making it a reliable, everyday hoodie that delivers serious quality without breaking the bank.

Cozy Earth’s hoodie has that sink-into-the-couch kind of comfort you get from the brand’s pajamas and sheets. It’s made from combed cotton and polyester, which is soft, supple, and weighted just right, giving it a drapey, almost cloud-like feel against the skin. Unlike Reigning Champ’s hoodie, which has a more structured build, Cozy Earth’s version feels more forgiving and relaxed like a wearable hug, perfect for lazy mornings in bed or weekend binge-watching sessions.

The subtle branding on the chest keeps the look minimal and versatile. Our editors note it has that weightless feel that makes you never want to take it off. Even without spandex, the hoodie lets us lift the suitcase into an overhead bin. Not to mention, its relaxed fit is perfect to layer underneath and wear on a flight as it tends to get cold on the aircraft. The inside has stayed plush wash after wash, while the outside keeps a smooth, lived-in softness that drapes neatly.

When the weather really goes rogue in the winter, Carhartt’s heavyweight hoodie might be your best defense. It’s seriously thick—built to take on wind, cold, and even a bit of drizzle, thanks to the durable water-repellent finish. Our editors noted how it shrugged off light rain on a walk to the gym without soaking through. Another editor wore it for a weekend cabin trip and said it kept him perfectly comfortable chopping wood outside in 40-degree weather. It feels insulated without weighing you down like a full-on parka. This is on brand for Carhartt, which specializes in producing durable workwear that can handle all sorts of conditions.

Instead of the hood being cut from one flat piece of fabric, it’s paneled to better contour to your head and neck, meaning it doesn’t bunch up or blow off when the wind picks up. The inside jersey lining feels soft like your favorite tee, and even with a beanie underneath the hood didn’t feel tight or floppy. We also love the deep front handwarmer pocket—it's great for thawing frozen hands or stashing gloves. Plus, there’s a hidden security pocket inside that’s perfect for stashing your phone or wallet.

The Reigning Champ Midweight Terry Standard Hoodie is built to last thanks to its 100 percent cotton 390 GSM (grams per square meter) fabric—midweight for a hoodie, meaning it feels substantial and durable without being too heavy. It’s soft against the skin yet holds its shape and resists pilling, even after half a dozen washes. I’ve worn mine on brisk morning walks, light workouts, and errands, and it still looks and feels like new.

This hoodie doesn’t skimp on details starting with the semi-raglan sleeves, which are a hybrid cut where the shoulder seams sit slightly off the top of your shoulder, giving you more freedom to move without that overly sporty look. Then there’s the dual-layer hood that adds structure and warmth—it’s made from two layers of fabric, so it actually keeps its shape and stays put instead of falling off. And the flatlock seams? They sit flush against your skin to cut down on bulk and rubbing, all while adding serious durability to prevent stretching out or fraying over time.

The midweight terry hits the sweet spot between structure and comfort: heavier than a Uniqlo hoodie but lighter than a full heavyweight pullover. Falling between slim and relaxed, it contours to the body without feeling tight, and I can easily layer a T-shirt or light long sleeve underneath. We found that this pick is universally flattering on all body types and has some structure that doesn’t feel too restrictive like most close-fitting hoodies. Plus, the hoodie can adapt to any casual setting, so you can transition from doing cardio to chowing down at the local food festival—without looking out of place.

Among the midweight hoodies we tested, Flint and Tinder’s style easily takes the crown. It hits that perfect balance between structure and softness; you get some weight and shape without the stiffness. This style is made from French terry, a cotton fabric known for its tiny loops on the inside that trap air and help regulate body temperature.

One tester said it kept them warm when the temps spiked but never felt stuffy when they were indoors or layering up. Most hoodies go too heavy and stiff or too thin and flimsy; this one lands right in the middle. The regular fit is not baggy or muscle-hugging, it sits comfortably on the shoulders and chest and drapes cleanly down the torso. It flatters guys with athletic builds but still leaves room to layer a tee or henley underneath without feeling bulky.

It’s also garment-dyed for that already broken-in feel right off the rack. The cotton feels dense yet plush, like a favorite sweatshirt that’s already been through a few perfect washes. In our testing, this hoodie held up beautifully. It didn’t stretch out at the cuffs or hem, and the color kept its rich tone even after multiple washes—a perk of the garment-dye process.

We wore it everywhere: morning coffee runs, cool evening walks, even to the office on casual Fridays. In fact, it’s one of those hoodies that can be worn year-round. Plus, the kangaroo pocket is deep enough to hold your phone, wallet, or even your hands when it’s brisk out.

Vuori is one of our favorite athleisure brands because it’s known for sweat-wicking basics that honor its laid-back SoCal roots. That’s why we love the Strato Tech Hoodie. Style Director Christian Gollayan ran five miles in it, and the polyester-elastane blend stayed relatively dry even by the fourth mile, with only minimal dampness by the time he finished. He didn’t feel so gross that he had to change before knocking out a grocery run.

The classic fit sits close to the body, so it contours to your shoulders and torso without feeling restrictive. Because of that close cut, you can comfortably wear a long sleeve, workout tee, or undershirt, but anything bulky will start to feel tight. The arms are cut narrow too, but thanks to the added stretch, you still get full mobility—though stacking too many layers on top can make the sleeve feel snug.

Gollayan was able to throw a gym bag over his shoulder and swing his arms while walking. Compared to Uniqlo’s fabric, this hoodie has a much thinner, lightweight layer you barely notice, but not so thin that it feels flimsy. The fabric is also incredibly soft, probably one of the softest on the list next to Cozy Earth.

Uniqlo’s built its reputation on timeless basics that feel just as current now as they will years from now—all without breaking the bank. Enter the brand’s oversized hoodie, which doesn’t swallow you, but feels soft, roomy, and easy to move in. The cotton-polyester fabric is sturdy and thick, but not heavy enough to make you feel you’re wearing a wool blanket on a mild day. Like Alo’s hoodie, it features dropped shoulders, where the seam falls lower on the arm and gives it a relaxed, roomy fit across the upper body. This way you can layer a crewneck or even a windbreaker.

The interior has a smooth texture that feels like a technical workout tee but with more structure. It’s not fluffy like a traditional hoodie yet it’s lightweight and breathable to wear in a muggy subway. I wore mine on a quick walk to the cafe, and unlike most bulky hoodies, I stayed cozy without breaking a sweat. The cut is longer, so I’d size down if you want it to fit a little more snug. Given how premium the fabric feels, you’d expect it to be pricier, but it’s reasonable enough to stock up on a couple at a time.

Beyond looking fly, Maison Wheat’s zip-up hoodie offers a lot of comfort and convenience. Unlike the pullovers on this list that’ll mess up your brushed hair, the full zipper makes it easy to take on and off. I like that you can zip it all the way up to my chin to trap heat on chilly mornings or leave it partially open to stay cool when it warms up. Because it opens completely, it layers cleanly under jackets or over heavier pieces—something most pullover hoodies can’t pull off without making you look stuffed.

What also sets this style apart is the Tencel modal fabric. It’s got that luxuriously five-star hotel sheet softness, drapey and smooth like a second skin. It’s lighter than fleece and French terry, but heavier and silkier than a basic cotton jersey, so it feels premium without the bulk. During our testing, we found it packs down easily into a suitcase and doesn’t take up any space. Yes, it’s more expensive than other options, but you’re paying for a high-quality piece that’s super versatile and feels great on the skin.

The best hoodies for men are produced from high-quality materials that will keep you warm and comfortable. Most styles are made of a mix of fabrics like cotton fleece, terry cloth, or a cotton-polyester blend. Look for a hoodie that's naturally breathable, feels good on the skin, and will last for years to come. If you work out in a sweatshirt, opt for a lighter option with moisture-wicking and quick-drying fabrics designed for layering.

Ideally, your hoodies shouldn't fit too tight, but they also shouldn't be too loose either. The fit should align with your lifestyle. Below, we've broken down the four most common types on the market:

This is your standard, go-to fit. It's not too tight or too loose, offering a comfortable amount of room without being baggy. It's versatile, working well for both casual wear and layering.

As the name suggests, this one's more fitted through the body and sleeves, giving a sleeker look. It's great for those who want a more streamlined, modern silhouette without all the extra bulk.

This fit gives you more room than regular, often with a slightly dropped shoulder or looser sleeves. It's comfortable and easygoing but still looks intentional, offering a bit of room to breathe without going full-on oversized.

This one's all about the dramatic, roomy look, intentionally loose with plenty of space in the body and sleeves for a laid-back streetwear-inspired vibe. It's perfect for layering or just lounging around in something super comfy.

Hoodies can range from lightweight to heavyweight fabrics depending on the weather conditions. Lightweight materials may be better for indoor use, while heavyweight fabrics are better for outdoor activities. So consider the fabric and bulk for your weather needs.

Our fashion team—led by Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, with the help of our longtime contributor Ted Stafford—brings decades of combined experience in men’s style, fit, and performance wear. Christian has spent a decade covering menswear and grooming, testing hundreds of pieces to find what actually works for real guys’ wardrobes. Stafford, who has over 20 years in the fashion industry, has styled most Men’s Health cover shoots, working with top athletes and celebrities to make sure every look translates on camera and in everyday life.

I bring my own background in testing and styling wardrobe essentials, wearing each hoodie through real scenarios like commutes, weekend errands, and workouts to see how they actually hold up. Together, we tested more than 40 hoodies across top brands like Alo, Uniqlo, and more. Each one was evaluated for comfort, construction, versatility, and longevity, because the best hoodies aren’t just about softness—they’re about how they move, wear, and last.

Hoodies are all about casual comfort, so don’t stray too far from that lane. Pairing one with other relaxed staples like jeans, chinos, or joggers keeps your look laid-back without appearing like you're trying too hard. We also love layering hoodies under winter coats for a balanced contrast.

Some of the hoodies on our list, including Alo's, have matching sweatpants and joggers if you're going for a full set. For a more elevated look, try a merino wool or cashmere hoodie, which instantly dress things up. And if you want something more classic and casual, stick with a 100% cotton hoodie—it's timeless and easy to wear year-round.

When it comes to layering, the trick to dressing up a hoodie is balancing its relaxed feel with something more structured. Think a blazer, bomber, or denim jacket. Even a sleek leather jacket or wool coat can take things up a notch.

#4941. The 10 Most Comfortable Bras, According to Style Editors

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

I’ve tested more bras than I can count as a style writer. And over the years, I’ve learned that comfort is a nonnegotiable—if it digs, pinches, or rides up, it doesn’t deserve a space in my drawer. The thing is, no two boobs are exactly alike (not even your own). One might sit higher, be fuller, or have a different shape than the other. So finding the right bra isn’t about hitting a standard size—it’s about understanding your body. According to Navya Mysore, MD, a primary care physician and Women’s Health advisor, the right bra boosts comfort, improves posture, and eases back pain by evenly distributing breast tissue. If your band rides up, your straps slide, or your underwire doesn’t lie flat, it’s a clear sign something’s off.

And if your usual size suddenly stops working? Totally normal. Bra fitter and undergarment educator Kimmay Caldwell says weight changes, hormone shifts, or your monthly cycle can impact your size. To make it trickier, some brands still use outdated sizing methods (like the “plus four” rule), while others go by your exact underbust. Bottom line: your size can change and vary between clothing brands.

All of that can make bra shopping feel like a bit of a minefield, which is exactly why I tested 20 different styles across fits, fabrics, and support levels to find the ones that are actually worth your money. These ten passed the wear test and then some, proving that comfort, support, and style actually can exist in one bra.

A bra should fit your body—not the other way around—and Knix totally got the memo with this one. It feels snug at first, but it softens and molds to your shape with every wear. What really impressed me was the fit because it almost feels custom, thanks to the ultra-thin foam that contours without adding volume.

Plus, the sleek fabric (a nylon-spandex blend) moves with you, feeling super smooth against the skin and breathable enough to wear for hours.

If you're after definition without the discomfort, this wire-free option def delivers. The molded cups lift and separate, while subtle side padding helps prevent spillage and sideboob. The result? A natural shape, no extra bulk, and no awkward lines under tighter tops. And with 99 sizes (!!) and eight colors, the options are actually inclusive.

The only downside? It’s not the best for high movement and workouts. I find myself adjusting it when I bend or move quickly. Still, for everyday comfort and a super flattering fit, this one’s a standout.

If you love the shape and support of a traditional bra but can't stand the feel of underwire, the Shapermint Essentials Sweetheart Wireless Contour Bra is your happy medium. It delivers a surprisingly lifted, rounded silhouette without a single wire digging into your ribs, making it my top pick for anyone who wants all-day comfort.

The lightly contoured foam cups provide just enough structure to prevent the dreaded uniboob, while the wide, stretchy band stays comfortably in place without pinching or rolling. The smooth, buttery fabric feels soft against the skin and disappears nicely under T-shirts and other fitted tops.

I was especially impressed by how supportive it feels for a wireless bra. It lifts and shapes without feeling restrictive, and the wider straps help distribute weight so your shoulders don't pay the price after hours of wear. It's one of those bras you forget you're wearing—which is pretty much the highest compliment I can give.

Push-up bras with underwires have a bad rep, and for good reason. They’re usually stiff, pokey, and downright uncomfortable. But after wearing this Maidenform bra for months (yes, months), I can confidently say it’s a major exception to the rule.

From the start, this bra felt different. The underwire doesn’t dig or jab, thanks to its soft, stretchy crochet lace that moves with you. The cups are unpadded but still offer that ideal medium support and lift, enough to give shape and a gentle push-up effect, but never so much that I feel squeezed or overly sculpted. It’s supportive without being suffocating, which is rare in the world of push-ups.And let’s talk about the straps. They’re fully adjustable and convertible, so whether I’m going for a classic or criss-cross fit, I can tweak the style to match my outfit. That kind of versatility makes it feel like you’re getting two bras in one (and who doesn’t love a multitasker?).The lift it gives is subtle but effective. It’s not the dramatic “hello, cleavage” kind of push-up, but more of a natural, perky boost that works under everything from tees to low-cut dresses. No spillage, just a flattering shape that makes me feel more confident in whatever I’m wearing. Bonus points for the range of styles: It comes in smooth fabric options to wear under clingy tees, and lace versions for when you want to have a little more fun.One of my biggest bra fears? The dreaded back and side bulge. But this bra’s smoothing side panels genuinely help—there’s no weird digging or over-compression, just a smooth, flattering fit that doesn’t fight with your body. Long story short: I tested it, I lived in it, and I’m keeping it in my regular rotation.

As someone who hates wearing bras (the wires, the bulk, the digging), this is the one I wear most. Made for fuller busts (DD+), the Cosabella Evolution Curvy Bralette lifts and shapes with lightly molded cups, no wires necessary.

“It’s the only bralette I’ve found that can actually support my chest without feeling restrictive,” says style contributor Lily Wohlner. The soft, stretchy fabric, made from a smooth microfiber that consists of 85 percent polyamide and 15 percent elastane, molds to your body, starting snug and quickly adapting for a custom-like fit. “I will say, mine have stretched a bit over the past few years, so it might be time to re-up,” she says.

This bra provides exceptional support for larger busts, even without a heavy-duty wire band. Instead, it makes use of an elasticized band that provides a surprisingly large amount of support without digging into the skin. It also has extra support at the sides to prevent spillage and to keep everything looking seamless, even under thin t-shirts and tight dresses.

The adjustable straps and underband stay put, and the side coverage smooths everything out—no spillage, no weird lines under shirts. It gives a natural, rounded shape that works under pretty much anything.

If you tend to scoop the girls into place to make them look perkier (a good trick!), this Cuup bra does the work for you. The rounded neckline and unlined, unpadded cups naturally lift and shape, while seamlessly extending into the straps for clean lines and a flattering fit.

It runs snug, but that’s what makes it so supportive—my boobs stay put and look perkier without any adjusting. The underwire is super lightweight and flexible, so there’s zero digging or poking there. I also love that the cups are unlined, because it makes the bra feel super lightweight and barely there.

The bra is made from a microfiber blend of polyamide and elastane, so it’s buttery-smooth, stretches with you while keeping its shape, and is ultra-breathable. It’s great for warm days since it feels like next to nothing on the skin and helps wick moisture away. The microfiber is also great for pairing with thin or tight tops, since it's basically undetectable under clothing—no lines in sight.

The straps are fully adjustable for a customizable lift, and even though the cups are thin, they still offer enough coverage to prevent any chilly-day surprises, IYKYK. Since the cups run a bit small, sizing up might be your best bet for full coverage.

The Honeylove CrossOver Bra is ultra-comfortable, smoothing, and supportive. The nylon and spandex blend feels soft and wearable for hours without digging into your skin while providing a completely seamless silhouette from every angle. I always wear this pick under thinner tops, tight dresses, and clingy sweaters because it creates a totally streamlined look under clothes while lifting the girls and supporting the underarm area and sides.

Plus, the bonded cradle under the bust mimics the structure of an underwire, delivering firm support without any poking or pinching. The full mesh overlay adds light compression and lift, adding to the sleek look.

“The CrossOver bra feels like a sports bra on, which is especially handy for women in search of something extra-comfortable (hi),” says contributor Korin Miller, who wore this bra every day for nearly a month to see how well it performed. She appreciates the flexible boning at the sides of the cups to prevent sideboob and bulging.

This bra also has one of the widest size ranges on our list, which is a major win. However, it does run a little big, so if you're between sizes, consider sizing down for the best fit.

Read More: Honeylove CrossOver Bra Review

Finding a lace bra that's actually comfortable—especially if you have a larger bust—can feel like a tall order, but the Bravissimo Millie Bra proves you don't have to sacrifice support for something pretty. It's my top pick for fuller busts thanks to its soft stretch lace cups, which mold to your shape for a flexible, barely-there feel instead of digging in or gaping.

Unlike stiff, scratchy lace bras, this one feels surprisingly comfortable from the first wear. The unpadded cups hug your breasts without adding bulk, while the stretchy lace adapts to your natural shape for a fit that feels supportive without being restrictive. The delicate floral lace also gives it an elevated, feminine look that's pretty enough to show off under a slightly unbuttoned blouse or low-cut top.

Meanwhile, the side sling creates a naturally lifted, forward shape, and if you wear a JJ or K cup, those sizes include additional lining for even more support where you need it most. The result is a flattering silhouette that feels secure without relying on heavy padding.

The only catch is that it's designed specifically for fuller busts, so sizing starts at a D cup.

The Natori Bliss Perfection Bra nails the perfect balance of comfort and structure. It feels light and flexible but keeps everything perfectly lifted and in place. No readjusting is needed halfway through the day, as is so often the case. That's thanks to the stretchy fabric, fully adjustable straps and band, and the strong yet plush underwire.

The smooth microfiber fabric (a nylon and spandex blend) feels buttery-soft against the skin, with just enough stretch to move as you do. Even the lace trim—sometimes a red flag for irritation—is whisper-smooth and lies flat under clothes. And while there’s an underwire, it’s so well-cushioned that it supports without poking or digging.

It’s the only underwire bra I don’t rip off the second I get home. It’s really the only bra I reach for when I head to the office or if I’m wearing a top that requires a little more lift and support for that flattering look. Style-wise, it looks as good as it feels. The lightly-lined cups create a natural, rounded shape that disappears under everything from fitted tees to silk blouses, and the smooth band keeps the silhouette seamless.

Our only con? It’s handwash only. I tried washing mine in a mesh laundry bag the first time it needed a clean, and while it wasn’t destroyed, it definitely pilled a bit.

If you have a smaller bust, you don't need a ton of padding to get a flattering fit—and the Journelle Victory Plunge Bra is proof. It's my top pick for A- to C-cups thanks to its lightly structured, unlined design that hugs your natural shape while disappearing under clothes.

The contoured cups mold to your body for a smooth, comfortable fit, and because they lie completely flat, there's no bunching or gaping to contend with. Despite having zero padding, the cups still provide full nipple coverage, so you get a sleek look under even the clingiest t-shirts without adding extra bulk.

I also appreciate that the plunge neckline works under just about everything, from V-necks to lower-cut tops, while the underwire offers just enough lift to create a naturally rounded shape. The result is polished and supportive without looking overly structured.

The only drawback is that it's best suited to smaller busts, as it doesn't offer the level of coverage or support many fuller busts need. But it is available up to a G cup if you’d like to try it out yourself.

If you love a deep V-neckline but hate when your bra peeks out, meet your new go-to: the Harper Wilde Bliss Triangle Bralette. It’s made with a flattering plunge that stays supportive and hidden under low-cut tops and dresses. I’ve worn it under everything from wrap dresses to tanks and it disappears under all of them. The triangle shape gives a natural lift—no wires, no padding, just your boobs but sliiightly perkier.

Comfort-wise, it lives up to the name. The modal fabric is buttery-soft and stretchy in that live-in-it kind of way. The band is wide and smooth, so it stays put without digging, and the adjustable straps let you customize the fit. It’s also lightweight enough to forget you’re even wearing it.

It’s become my go-to for daily wear, and the super-soft, barely-there material is truly the next best thing to going bra-free. While it’s equally great for bed-rotting or taking Zoom calls from home, I also feel confident wearing it out and about because it doesn’t skimp on coverage and offers just enough support.

Even without padding, the double-layered fabric gives solid nipple coverage. It comes in inclusive sizes and neutral shades that go with everything. The few cons? It’s not super supportive for heavy movement or fuller busts, so you may need to readjust on the go. But for everyday wear, especially with low-cut outfits, it fits the bill.

The most comfortable bras usually come down to the right blend of fabrics. Here’s what each one brings to the table:

Comfort is about more than just size—it’s also about ensuring the wire doesn’t create pressure points or cause discomfort throughout the day. Look for bras with flexible, padded, or cushioned underwires, which offer support without digging into your skin. The underwire should sit flat against your ribcage and follow the natural curve of your breasts. If it feels like it’s poking or shifting, it’s not the right fit. If you prefer a wire-free bra, opt for styles with flexible boning, molded cups, and wide, flexible bands to provide support.

The most accurate way to find your size is to get fitted in person. Once you have your size, your new bra should feel snug and secure. The band should be comfortably tight, but not dig into the skin. A good rule of thumb is that you should be able to fit two fingers between the band and your skin, but no more. The cups should also lie flat against your chest.

The Women’s Health team has been testing bras since we first wrote this story in 2023. To find the most comfortable options, our team wore each style for at least a few weeks at a time. We wore them under different circumstances, including workouts, lounging, and long days at the office. But our main criterion for each bra was comfort. I also spoke with two bra experts and personally tested 20-plus bras over several years to lock down the ones I actually wear on repeat.

I recently re-tested a bunch of options and tapped style contributor Lily Wohlner for an update to this story to boost our list and keep it up-to-date. The final guide includes everything from bralettes and seamless bras to push-up bras—and I actually wear all of them in my day-to-day life.

#4939. Emideltide Keeps Getting a ‘No’ for Compounding. What’s the Problem?

Why the government’s renewed interest in peptides excludes this one.

THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION has not been shy about its pro-peptide stance. US Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has pushed to make six popular yet unapproved peptides available for compounding to people with a prescription. A recent FDA advisory committee meeting voted in favor of adding six out of seven peptides to a list of substances that U.S. compounding pharmacies are allowed to manufacture and supply.

Six out of seven. So what happened to that last peptide? Emideltide, also dubbed DSIP, is a peptide people have turned to for better sleep. And it was the only peptide the FDA advisory board voted against moving out of the Category 2 list—a substance considered to carry significant safety risks, with compounding pharmacies prohibited from making it. Here’s why.

EMIDELTIDE IS A nine-amino-acid peptide originally isolated from the blood of sleeping rabbits during electrically induced sleep in the late 1970s. Since its discovery, a synthetic peptide version has been administered via injection or a nasal spray.

Emideltide reportedly helps you fall asleep faster and extend the time spent in deep sleep. It’s also been used to avoid waking up multiple times throughout the night and anecdotal reports online have mentioned more vivid, Inception–like lucid dreaming. With better sleep, people online using emideltide have mentioned feeling less stress, more refreshed upon waking, and faster recovery after a grueling workout.

MOST RESEARCH LOOKING into the peptide’s role in sleep, however, took place in the 1980s and 1990s—with mixed findings.

For example, a 1984 case study reported on a 35-year-old guy with 10 years of narcolepsy who had reduced sleep attacks, less daytime napping, and more alertness with weekly emideltide injections administered in the morning.

One clinical trial had 16 people take an emideltide injection or a placebo while measuring how long it took for them to fall asleep once they’re tucked into bed. People who had an emideltide injection said they felt more tired and actually went to sleep quicker than the placebo group. That should be great except when they repeated the experiment a second night, the placebo group knocked out quicker than the peptide group.

Another study in 1992 found the peptide helped chronic insomniacs feel less tired. However, there was such little difference in the time it took to fall asleep and stay asleep in the emideltide group versus the placebo group. The authors of the 1992 study said any small improvements with the peptide were probably “due to an incidental change in the placebo group” and “not likely to be of major therapeutic benefit.”

BEYOND SLEEP, EMIDELTIDE has been explored in animal studies for potentially protecting against cancer and improving motor ability after stroke. Another realm of interest is how emideltide might help with curbing withdrawal after addiction.

A 1984 study found emideltide injections helped reduce the severity of opioid withdrawal symptoms in 97 percent of people with addiction along with alcohol withdrawal symptoms in 87 percent of people with alcohol addiction. Although more peptide injections were needed in people with opiate addiction.

In 1998, researchers gave a single injection of emideltide to seven people with opioid dependence. While they reported improvements in opioid withdrawal, the team also noted “it remains an open question whether DSIP could be an effective alternative detoxification approach.” Some of the issues were the small sample size, lack of a placebo group for proper comparison, and that each person knew they were getting an emideltide injection. The lack of randomization makes it hard to say for sure that a treatment actually worked or if people subjectively felt better because they knew they were getting treatment.

WE KNOW EMIDELTIDE doesn’t act like a sedative that slows down the brain and body’s function. But how the peptide exactly works is still up for debate.

The peptide is often considered a sleep-regulator rather than a suppressant. We know emideltide doesn’t act like a sedative or sleeping pill that slows down the brain and body’s function. But how the peptide exactly works is still up for debate.

One possible mechanism is that the peptide increases delta-wave activity. These are your slowest brain waves at 0.5 to 4 Hz that are indicative of deep sleep. Deep sleep is linked to better memory, energy, and all that good stuff you get from a good night’s sleep. There may also be some neuroendocrine effects going on that could explain why people feel calm enough to pass out. A small study back in the ’80s injected a single dose of emideltide in 11 guys and found lower levels of ACTH, a hormone that stimulates your adrenal glands to release the stress hormone cortisol (though this mechanism has been disputed).

The FDA advisory meeting relied on studies that focused on emideltide’s cross-talk with the opioid system in the brain. While the peptide doesn’t directly interact with opioid receptors, evidence points to emideltide somehow being able to trigger the release of endorphins. This may also provide painkiller properties (which is why it’s been proposed as a way to suppress alcohol and opioid withdrawal syndrome).

EMIDELTIDE WILL PROBABLY stay banned—and found only through the sketchy gray market—because there’s not enough information to know if emideltide might do more harm than good.

Since emideltide interacts with the opioid system, there is a possibility that it could lead to addiction. Right now, there are no animal or human studies that prove emideltide wouldn’t worsen addictive behaviors.

There’s also not enough data on whether repeated emideltide use would cause other safety issues. While the small sleep trials did not report any serious side effects, withdrawal studies noted headaches, nausea, and vertigo. After the second injection, some had low blood pressure although the researchers also said it’s unclear whether those symptoms were because of the peptide or from withdrawal altogether.

Jocelyn Solis-Moreira, MS is the associate health & fitness for Men's Health and has previously written for CNN, Scientific American, Popular Science, and National Geographic before joining the brand. When she's not working, she's doing circus arts or working towards the perfect pull-up.

#4938. Bitcoin Wallet Maker Trezor Says Customer Data Was Exposed Again

Bitcoin Wallet Maker Trezor Says Customer Data Was Exposed Again

The “days since last third-party breach” counter at Trezor has reset to zero once again.

This time, hackers accessed shipping partner Skladon's systems and likely exported information tied to approximately 27,000 hardware-wallet orders, according to a company disclosure published Monday.

The intrusion occurred November 7, but Skladon did not notify Trezor until November 15. The exposed records cover orders placed between August 9 and November 7, including customers' full names, phone numbers, delivery and email addresses, plus the products they bought and their prices.

Trezor said its own systems were not compromised, and no wallet backups, PINs or passphrases were involved. The breach does not, by itself, let an attacker move a buyer's coins, but it gives them a potentially dangerous combination: a home address and evidence that someone bought a device designed to store crypto.

The latest incident follows an August shipping partner hack and a September email provider breach, making three separate third-party security incidents in a little over three months.

Trezor said some customers have already reported fraudulent phone calls. Criminals could cite the exact model and price of a wallet to make an unsolicited call, text or letter seem legitimate, or use a home address to identify someone who may hold cryptocurrency.

In August, logistics provider ShipMonk suffered a breach that initially appeared to affect fewer than 14,000 Trezor customers. An updated investigation uncovered records for another 67,000 U.S. buyers from 2019 to 2021 that ShipMonk had retained despite assurances they had been deleted, bringing the total to 80,689 people.

September brought another incident, this time at marketing email provider Brevo. Hackers used Trezor's legitimate email channel to distribute a fake security warning urging recipients to install an app that requested their wallet backups. Trezor later said 347,149 email addresses had been exported.

These weren't Trezor's first brushes with the problem. A Mailchimp insider attack targeted Trezor users in 2022, and a 2024 breach of its external support portal put the contact details of up to 66,000 people at risk.

The fallout can go beyond inbox spam. In February, fake letters were sent to hardware-wallet owners, complete with Trezor branding, holograms and QR codes leading to phishing sites.

Asked why an order from Trezor's official store involved an outside company, Trezor responded that it’s basically a logistics question, not a tech issue. “Companies of our size and global reach can’t run efficiently without third-party service providers,” the company replied to a comment on X.

Hi, companies of our size and global reach can’t run efficiently without third-party service providers. Handling as much as possible internally is the goal, but doing every part of the business ourselves isn’t realistic. Skladon is one of the partners that delivers Trezor orders,…

It said Skladon held only the information needed to deliver parcels, and handling every stage of global distribution in-house was not realistic.

Trezor says Skladon does not ship to the United States, so American buyers were not affected by this incident. Affected customers have been notified where possible, though some people who ordered between August 9 and 14 may not receive an email because Trezor had already anonymized their records.

The company has introduced anonymous pickup at parcel lockers or collection points in 18 European countries, allowing buyers to avoid supplying a home address. It is also working to shorten retention of order data from 90 to 45 days and says shipping partners will have to follow the same policy.

Trezor advises customers to ignore unexpected calls and messages about their orders, check any concerns through its official support site and never share a wallet backup. It has notified a data protection authority, but has not yet disclosed how attackers got into Skladon's systems.

#4937. Boris Johnson says UK must lead blockchain development despite crypto doubts

Johnson was joined by Lord Ross Kempsell who called for regulators to work with industry participants to bring the UK to the forefront.

Former United Kingdom Prime Minister Boris Johnson has backed blockchain technology and tokenization as opportunities for the UK’s financial sector, despite persistent doubts about cryptocurrencies.

Speaking at Solana’s Breakpoint conference in London on Monday, Johnson maintained his position that Bitcoin (BTC) resembles a Ponzi scheme, following an opinion piece published in the Daily Mail in March. He questioned who investors could hold accountable if funds were stolen.

However, Johnson distinguished his criticism of digital assets from his view of the underlying technology, saying the UK should be at the forefront of tokenization.

Lord Ross Kempsell, who joined Johnson on stage, said although he shared his reservations on cryptocurrencies, “on the parts of the industry that can be brought into a regulated perimeter, which the regulators are working on, there’s a lot of scope here for a high growth industry.”

Kempsell, whom Johnson nominated for a peerage in 2022, told the panel that more than 8% of UK adults hold crypto, in line with Financial Conduct Authority-commissioned research published in December 2025.  Speaking to Cointelegraph after his stage appearance, he said, “I’m a very big believer in making London and keeping London as the onchain capital for innovation.”

Related: UK financial watchdog opens consultations for DeFi guidance, crypto laws

He argued that consumer protection and financial innovation should not be treated as competing priorities, pointing to the UK’s established fintech industry as an example of how regulation can coexist with innovation in the country. He said the UK should avoid introducing a single, all-encompassing piece of crypto legislation, opting instead for “a more ad-hoc approach” to regulation.

He called for collaboration between the regulators and market participants to understand both the risks and opportunities. While he saw consumer protection as “paramount,” he felt it was unfair to single out the crypto industry as the only sector where consumer protection was at risk.

“Really what I care about is the economic growth potential that there is in this industry, the job creation potential, and also its wider links to tech, AI and traditional financial innovation. London’s always been at the center of those historically,” Kempsell told Cointelegraph.

When asked about the approach of the current administration in the UK, he highlighted that “they need to make sure that they get the fundamental market conditions right.” In his eyes, that meant making the UK a competitive player in regard to tax and facilitating business innovation.

Related: UK names 6 banks to lead first digitally native government bond

Tim Meggs, co-founder of London-based digital asset trading firm Lo:Tech, said Johnson “made a fair point about people getting burned,” but said most of the losses experienced by the industry stemmed from thin liquidity and a lack of visibility over how prices were made.

“If the FCA gets its perimeter right, the UK has a chance to make that kind of transparency the norm,” Meggs said. “But until the clearing and prime broking infrastructure catches up, good rules won’t be enough on their own to make London the place where serious digital asset trading gets done.”

Robin Nordnes, founder and CEO of Solana infrastructure firm Raiku, argued that Johnson’s question about who is in charge makes the case for blockchain, since a public ledger needs no guarantor. “Every transaction on Solana is public and can be checked by anyone, which is more than you can say for most of what happens in the City,” he said.

Nordnes warned that “if Westminster keeps treating this as retail speculation, the trading systems behind the next generation of markets will be built in New York and Singapore, and London will end up renting them.”

#4934. The 9 Best Sweaters for Men, Tested by Style Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

From classic cotton crews to cozy cashmere, every knit is here.

I’LL ADMIT IT: sweaters are my kryptonite. Long before I was a style editor, they were my secret weapon. In my early twenties, I realized that a well-cut knit could elevate a look more effortlessly than any blazer or jacket. I’ve worn them through newsroom winters, weekend getaways, and way too many cold subway commutes to count. Growing up, I’d watch Pharrell Williams turn a simple crewneck into a statement, marvel at Andre 3000’s fearless layering, and admire A$AP Rocky’s ability to make a chunky sweater feel cool. Those moments have stuck with me, teaching me that style isn’t about what you wear but how you wear it. Sweaters became my canvas—and they still are, whether I’m braving the elements or dressing to impress.

Since 2020, the Men’s Health style team and I have tested more than 50 styles—crewnecks, cable knits, turtlenecks—to find the ones that actually deliver. Sweaters are also one of my go-to holiday gifts since they’re practical and available at just about every price point. Ahead, you’ll find our top picks that check every box, whether you’re shopping for yourself or grabbing dad a new knit for the season.

I’ve been testing men’s sweaters since 2020, so as you can imagine, I’ve worn more than I can count. Polo Ralph Lauren’s cable-knit has consistently risen above the competition in construction, fit, and timeless style. The brand helped cement the cable-knit as an American preppy classic, and that history shows in the sweater itself. The textured braids and patterns give it depth and richness, elevating even the simplest outfit. You can see and feel the heritage in every stitch—the weight, the structure, the classic lines all signal a piece built to last.

The relaxed fit is a major win for comfort—it offers extra room in the chest, which is perfect if you’ve got bigger pecs (like me, after a few years of lifting). Even without spandex, it layers beautifully over a button-up without stretching out or losing its shape. During testing, I wore it over a crisp white dress shirt for a dinner party, under a blazer for a Zoom meeting, and casually with joggers on a morning matcha latte run. The fabric feels soft against the skin but maintains structure. It never made me break a sweat, and kept me cozy in temps in the high 50s. I’ve washed mine over six times, and the sweater still looks and fits like new.

I also love how it pairs seamlessly with a variety of pants—tailored trousers, jeans, and casual sweats all work. And of course, that unmistakable Ralph Lauren heritage baked in, giving a sense of legacy that many sweaters lack. One thing to keep in mind: it comes with a premium price tag, which might be a barrier, only if you’re looking for a budget-friendly option that won’t exude as much style.

Amazon Essentials offers everything from the best men’s basics to sharp sweaters, and this one’s proof that affordable doesn’t mean cheaply made. This V-neck style is breathable in the winter, easy to layer, and feels surprisingly premium for the price. Our editors wore it under blazers and sport coats, and then over a crisp shirt with the collar peeking. (Don’t wear it with a T-shirt unless you’re going for a laid-back look). The regular fit is relaxed–but-not-boxy, and forgiving if you’ve just had a burger.

The 100 percent cotton knit feels soft against the skin with just the right amount of stretch, so there’s no restriction when I raise my arms or reach for my coffee. Given its price, you’d think it would become dingy after a few wears or washes, but that’s not the case. Despite months of wear and multiple wash cycles, it held its shape without fading or pilling. Bonus: it comes in a range of colors and argyle prints, so you can stock up and keep your office fits in rotation.

If outdoor running is part of your winter routine, you should consider Vuori’s Performance Crew. It’s designed with both comfort and functionality in mind. Made from a stretchy, moisture-wicking fabric, it keeps you dry and moves with you, whether you’re running errands or working up a sweat. The brand’s signature DreamKnit fabric feels like velvet and won’t overheat you when layered over a lightweight T-shirt or tank top. It's by far the smoothest, most buttery-soft fabric we’ve ever tested. With a modern athletic fit, the cut follows the natural shape of your body without being too tight or loose. You still have the freedom of movement while still looking put-together, so it’s perfect for intense workouts and casual wear.

A good cashmere sweater feels like wrapping yourself in a cloud, and Naadam’s version is one that our style team can’t get enough of. The first time I pulled it on, I understood why: it’s ridiculously soft—way softer than regular wool so it feels amazing against my skin without any itching. It’s lightweight too, so you don’t overheat when the radiator’s on full blast, but still warm enough for windy commutes.

After a few wears, I noticed it never lost its shape and didn’t pill as fast as cheaper cashmere sweaters I’ve tested (a small miracle at this price). Keep in mind: cashmere is delicate, so this one requires more care than cotton or polyester sweaters. I’m also a fan of how many colors they offer, including cobalt and tangerine that really stand out without being loud. For guys with athletic builds, it’s the perfect cut. It skims your frame just right, showing off your shoulders and giving your biceps a little spotlight. Just note: sizes do run small, so if you’re between sizes, go up.

I’ve tested a bunch of budget knits, but this one from Uniqlo punches way above its price tag. The cotton-blend fabric feels soft straight out of the package and has a tight ribbed construction that keeps its shape after a dozen washes, and somehow still looks brand new. Although it doesn’t have the weight or the luxe feel of higher-end knits, I’ve worn this for months and found no fading, stretching, or weird pilling.

The synthetic blend gives it that smooth, premium hand-feel with a bit of stretch, so you can reach, twist, and move without feeling boxed in. I also love how the fit strikes that sweet spot between tailored and relaxed—it skims the body without clinging, which makes it look sharp enough for the office but laid-back enough for Sunday coffee runs. The ribbing on the collar keeps it in shape and adds a subtle texture, providing a durable and neat finish. And since it’s machine washable, you can toss it in with your regular laundry and forget about dry cleaning.

I’ve always loved turtleneck sweaters—they’re dressier and provide more coverage than your standard crewneck. But if you’re on the shorter or leaner side, a full turtleneck can sometimes feel like too much fabric stacked around your neck. Suitsupply’s roll neck solves that problem perfectly. It delivers the same refined look and warmth of a turtleneck, just with less bulk so you don’t need a scarf. I found it especially handy during the freezing winter mornings. The merino wool breathes surprisingly well, so I didn’t overheat when layering it under a blazer or waiting for the train in a muggy subway station.

You can skip a trip to the dry cleaners because the fabric is tough enough to handle a spin in the washer and come out looking sharp with zero shrinkage or sagging. Plus, it’s odor-resistant, so I stayed fresh from my morning commute through my evening dinner. What I love the most is the versatility. Thanks to its minimalistic look, I’ve layered it under everything from a bomber jacket for errands to a tailored suit for a fancy holiday party. Whether you’re going for laid-back or dress-to-impress, this turtleneck fits the bill perfectly. The slim fit is clean but not constricting—enough to streamline my upper body without being tight, and yes, it gives the pecs a nice little lift. Guys with bigger chests or arms may have to size up for a comfortable fit.

This ribbed crew is one of those pieces that just feels right from the first wear. It’s made from a richly textured cotton rib that gives it some real weight—thicker than your average knit but never stiff or bulky. The texture adds that broken-in look while the classic fit keeps things clean and flattering. It sits close to the body without squeezing you, which makes it great for guys with broader shoulders who want structure, and it gives slimmer builds a sharper, more defined shape. It drapes cleanly through the shoulders and arms, and has just enough give whether you’re layering it under a jacket or reaching for something on a shelf.

What really sets it apart from other sweaters is the feel—it’s got that hearty, hand-knit texture you usually only get from a vintage find, but it wears lighter and breathes better than heavy wool. After its first wash, the ribbing softened up so much we wanted to wear it three days in a row. The look lands somewhere between rugged fisherman and clean-cut. Yeah, it’s not cheap, but the rich construction, flattering fit, and durability make it worth the investment.

If you’re going to wear a sweater, make sure it’s in a classic color that won’t feel dated after one season. This style comes in a nice red or grey that are bold enough to stand out but not overwhelming that you’ll regret it in photos later. It plays well with dressier trousers for a dinner or intimate gathering. The unique ribbing along the sides, neckline, and hem gives it some nice texture, while the standard fit hits that sweet spot between relaxed and put-together. It might feel a bit boxy if you prefer a more tailored, close-to-the-body look.

The merino wool and nylon fabric blend feels sturdy but not stiff—it’s thick enough to keep you warm on chilly mornings but breathable once you’re indoors. One of our testers even wore it on a coffee run and didn’t break a sweat under a jacket. It’s got just the right amount of stretch too, so you can move around without feeling like you're trapped in a knit straitjacket. The vibe is rugged but still polished, which means it works just as well with jeans and clean sneakers, as well as with tailored trousers and loafers.

I’ve been wearing this cashmere quarter-zip from Quince for a few weeks now, and it’s one of those sweaters that makes you realize how nice cashmere can actually feel. The fisherman rib knit gives it real heft and structure, so it feels premium the second you pull it on. This one is made from Mongolian cashmere, which has longer, finer fibers, so it's ten times softer and more durable. You’re basically getting that luxury feel for a budget-friendly price point. It has a classic fit but is trim enough that it doesn’t bunch up when you sit or layer it under a coat or over a button-down.

I wore this during New York City’s shoulder season, and it regulated temperature really well. I never got hot walking to work or felt chilly when the office AC kicked on. The fabric breathes better than most wool sweaters I’ve tested, and it never got that itchy, fuzzy feeling that cashmere can sometimes pick up after a few wears. Plus, the quarter-zip collar gives it versatility, too: zipped up, it looks sharp for the office; unzipped, it leans casual for the weekend. You can choose from a range of easy-to-wear neutral tones; think navy, black, and charcoal, which all pair effortlessly with chinos or dark jeans.

Look for high-quality materials that ensure warmth, comfort, and longevity. By understanding what each fabric brings to the table, you can select the sweater that fits both your lifestyle and your wardrobe goals. Here’s a closer look at what you can expect from the most common options:

Cashmere is the gold standard for softness and luxury. It’s made from the undercoat of cashmere goats, resulting in an ultra-fine, buttery fabric. Expect it to feel lightweight yet warm, perfect for layering without adding bulk. Cashmere sweaters often have a higher price tag, but their timeless appeal and plush feel make them a worthwhile investment. Just remember: cashmere requires delicate care, like handwashing or dry cleaning, to maintain its softness.

Merino wool is a performance powerhouse. Derived from Merino sheep, this wool is fine, soft, and naturally moisture-wicking, making it ideal for regulating body temperature. Merino wool sweaters keep you warm without overheating and are often odor-resistant, so they’re great for active or travel-heavy lifestyles. Bonus: Many are machine washable, adding a dose of convenience.

Cotton sweaters are breathable, lightweight, and perfect for transitional weather or layering indoors. They’re soft on the skin and great for those who find wool too itchy. Cotton doesn’t retain as much heat as wool, so it’s best suited for milder climates or casual settings. Expect easy care—most cotton sweaters are machine washable.

Blended fabrics combine the best of both worlds. For example, wool-cashmere blends deliver the softness of cashmere with the durability of wool, while wool-cotton blends offer a balance of warmth and breathability. These blends are often more affordable and easier to care for than pure fibers.

Alpaca wool is soft, silky, and hypoallergenic—great for those with sensitive skin. It’s warmer than regular wool but feels lighter, making it perfect for chilly days without feeling too heavy. Alpaca sweaters often have a natural luster, giving them a polished, luxurious look.

The best sweaters for men should strike the perfect balance—tailored enough to look polished, but comfortable enough for all-day wear. Pay attention to the shoulder and chest areas, which should be roomy enough for an undershirt or a button-down shirt underneath, but also not too loose and still snug and slim enough for looking elevated during standalone wear. Sleeves should hit at the wrist bone when your arms are relaxed at your sides and the overall silhouette should be neither too tight nor too loose. A well-fitting sweater not only enhances your style but also maximizes comfort and complements your body shape.

Opt for designs that work across settings, whether it’s a classic crewneck for casual days, a half-zip for sporty outings, or a cable-knit for a dressier touch. A great sweater should transition with no problem from every location to the next.

Between Style Director Christian Gollayan, who’s spent the past decade covering men’s fashion, and me, who’s tested sweaters, jackets, and everything in between over the past five years, we’ve worn enough knits to fill an entire coat check. Together, we pulled on dozens of sweaters in every fit, fabric, and price point to see which ones actually live up to the hype. We wore them to the office, out to dinner, on weekend errands, and through too many cold commutes. We paid close attention to how each sweater fit (flattering or frumpy?), how it felt against the skin (buttery soft or scratchy mess?), how it held up after a wash, and whether it layered neatly without bulk. After plenty of wear, tear, and mirror checks, we narrowed it down to the sweaters that truly earn their keep—sharp, comfortable, durable, and ready for anything winter throws your way.

The key lies in understanding the different styles of sweaters and pairing them accordingly for various occasions. For a casual, laid-back look that you can wear every day, try a classic crewneck sweater with your go-to pants—perfect for running errands or grabbing coffee with friends. V-neck sweaters are ideal for smart-casual or business-casual settings, whether you're at the office or at dinner, since they layer beautifully over collared shirts. (Zip sweaters also work as such, by the way.)

Cardigan sweaters are easy to dress up: layer a button-down shirt beneath a well-fitted cardigan for a sophisticated, professional-looking appearance, or pair them with khakis and tailored trousers to achieve a preppy look. Similarly, turtlenecks exude refinement and work for cocktail and business-casual attire, easily paired with tailored trousers and blazers for a polished, upscale look. For a more rugged, outdoorsy vibe, opt for a chunky cable knit or fisherman sweater.

#4933. ‘The Gilded Age’ Star Ben Ahlers and Todd Snyder Know the Power of a Good Uniform

For the label’s latest campaign, the 30-year-old actor takes fall style to Scotland’s Isle of Islay.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

TODD SNYDER makes some of our favorite menswear, and for its latest collaboration, the New York brand crossed the pond to Scotland. The draw? Lagavulin, the distillery that’s been making smoky Scotch whisky on the island of Islay for more than 200 years.

The partnership marks Snyder’s 15th anniversary, with clothes that borrow from Islay’s rugged landscape. Standouts include a brown suede jacket lined in Lagavulin’s own tartan and Fair Isle zip-ups in the earthy shades of the Scottish moors. Pretty great reasons to look forward to sweater weather.

Fronting the campaign is Ben Ahlers. As footman-turned-businessman Jack Trotter on The Gilded Age, the 30-year-old actor knows his way around heritage menswear. Still, these relaxed layers are pretty easy to picture on the streets of New York. We caught up with him about what playing Jack taught him about getting dressed—and which piece he’d bring home.

MEN’S HEALTH: You spend a lot of time in period costumes on The Gilded Age. Has anything from Jack’s wardrobe made its way into how you dress off-screen?

BEN AHLERS: Jack has a consistency to the way that he dresses. As a footman, he had a uniform, and as a young businessman, he has a pretty steady throughline through his looks—a base structure with really well-made clothing and then accents like a tie or a tie pin or a ring that can allow for a sense of creative expression. I find that I like a level of consistency in my own personal dress as well.

More than anything, the greatest benefit of living inside of the clothing that Kasia [Walicka Maimone, the show’s costume designer] and her incredible team make for us every year is this awareness of the way clothes not only make you present to the world but also how they make you feel within them.

MH: Is there a menswear trend from that era you wish more guys would embrace today?

BA: I would love to see some of the creativity come out in menswear and in the accent work, like a tie pin. Some of the tie pins we have on this show are just so well-crafted and specific. The heads of canes the men wore back then also have such an artistry to them, and there aren’t a lot of avenues for that sort of expression in modern menswear. It’d be nice to see that creative voice or risk-taking come through in the subtle accents that we wear in our day-to-day life.

MH: Your role in Death of a Salesman got people talking about your physique. How did you prepare?

BA: For Death of a Salesman, I knew earlier on in the development process that they wanted to go the direction that they did for the top of the show, and so I knew that I was going to be kind of exposed every night. I really tried to go to the gym during the rehearsal process because I knew once we opened the show that it was going to be hard to stay as active—the show was just so draining.

The couple of months up to opening, I really made a practice of five days a week of cross-training, lifting, running, and yoga, and trying to keep my body as nimble and buoyant as possible, because the subject matter and the daily grind of showing up to the theater every day can really take a toll.

During the run, a lot of my focus was on rest, recovery, sauna, cold plunge, diet, stretching, because I’d already built the foundation of the physicality. Throughout the five-month run, it came down to being sure that I was healthy and recovering as best as I could.

MH: What happened between takes on the Todd Snyder shoot that we’d never know from looking at the campaign photos?

BA: Between takes, I had a blast with Boo George, our photographer. He is such a character and one of the best energies on set, and really delivered in the work. The whole crew from Todd Snyder and Lagavulin were so supportive, and it was such a fun little escape for all of us to exist on this island in the most beautiful landscape imaginable.

I really enjoyed getting to know a lot of the locals there. Many of the people there worked at the distillery, and I got to see firsthand how the whisky was actually made. People were so proud to share their culture as well as their craft with the world.

MH: Which piece from the collection would you wear back home in New York, and what would you pair it with?

BA: My favorite piece from the collection is the Todd Snyder x Lagavulin suede stable jacket, inspired by the texture and color of the mossy peat that coats Islay. It’s a perfect fall jacket, and I’d pair it with Todd Snyder’s relaxed barrel jean in khaki, which I think would really pop.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

#4932. 6 Best Scalp Moisturizers, Tested by Editors and Dermatologists

Our top overall pick to fix a dry, itchy scalp is a budget-friendly serum from The Ordinary.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

A dry, itchy scalp can seriously mess with your day-to-day life. Beyond the maddening urge to scratch, there's the embarrassing component: dandruff and big white flakes studding your strands. And while dermatologists say that a dry, flaking scalp may be a sign of a medical condition called seborrheic dermatitis (this requires a prescription treatment like Zoryve), the best scalp moisturizers—hydrating shampoos for dry scalp, conditioners, and serums—can help.

"I always recommend starting with a gentle, sulfate-free shampoo that cleanses without stripping the scalp of its natural oils and following that up with a hydrating conditioner," says Ross Kopelman, MD, a hair transplant surgeon at Kopelman Hair Restoration in New York City. You can then follow that up with a leave-in treatment or a scalp oil to really lock in moisture.

It's also a good idea to limit hair washing to two to three times a week. "I suggest washing your hair with lukewarm water instead of hot and avoiding excessive heat styling, which can make things worse," Kopelman says. Before adding a few scalp moisturizers to your routine, here's what you should consider before shopping.

Below, shop the six best scalp moisturizers for all hair types, tested by editors and beauty experts.

The Women's Health team is regularly testing scalp moisturizers, and we found it's hard to beat this scalp serum from The Ordinary because of the exceptional value it offers. Yes, it's well-priced, but both dermatologists and testers alike love it. "It's great because it uses hyaluronic acid to deeply hydrate without being greasy," Dr. Kopelman says. He also notes that it's suitable for all hair types, including fine, medium, and thick hair, whether straight, wavy, curly, or coily.

Since I find myself constantly scratching my scalp throughout the day, I added this scalp serum to my hair routine, and after a few days of using it, I found that my symptoms significantly improved. Plus, as an added bonus, my thick, wavy hair appeared shinier and felt softer.

Our testers also like that this The Ordinary product is a leave-in treatment, too, since that makes application quick and easy (meaning there's no need to only use it on wash day).

This drugstore pick is another very well-priced scalp moisturizer that dermatologists say really works. "It has aloe, which soothes the skin, green tea extract, which contains antioxidants, and peptides, which help make the scalp skin healthy," says Morgan Rabach, MD, a dermatologist in New York City. It also has plenty of benefits for your hair: It enhances shine, reduces frizz, adds body, and helps prevent split ends.

Like our top overall pick, this is a convenient leave-in treatment. Users like the tingly sensation from the eucalyptus leaf extract, too, telling WH it not only feels refreshing but also smells great.

Our editors can't get enough of Briogeo's hair products—from the shampoo to hair masks, we love just about everything the brand puts out. This scalp moisturizer is no exception. It's powered by antioxidant-rich rosemary oil that supports scalp circulation and healthier hair follicles, castor oil for hydration, and tea tree to fight flakes and reduce itchiness. It's also formulated with bisabolol to calm irritation from an itchy scalp.

We love that you can tailor the treatment to suit your preferences—use it as a pre-shampoo rinse (a wait time of 10 to 15 minutes) or use it as an overnight hair mask. Either way, testers found the pointed tip on the bottle very easy to use, saying it made for a much more precise application.

Living Proof makes another fantastic leave-in treatment for dry scalps. Like our top overall pick, it's hyaluronic acid-based to offer lightweight (read: won't leave hair greasy) but intense hydration. It also contains vitamin B3 to help improve overall scalp health.

The product is easy to use, thanks to a precise applicator tip. And there's no rinsing required, so you can more seamlessly integrate it into your routine. Users say it works quickly, minimizing symptoms in just a few uses and almost completely eradicating any itchiness and flakes in just about two weeks. They love the smell, too—some say it's reminiscent of the ocean.

Dr. Rabach is also a fan of Moroccanoil's Dry Scalp Treatment, namely because it contains argan oil. "It contains both vitamin E and antioxidants," she says. It also contains salicylic acid, which is a gentle exfoliator that helps lift any flakes and can prevent scalp buildup that could lead to itchiness and more flakes in the future. Geranium oil also helps soothe the scalp and addresses any lingering dryness.

Like other Moroccanoil products, users overwhelmingly rave about this scalp treatment, saying it's hydrating, soothing, and smells great. We also love that a little bit goes a long way, which helps add to the overall value of the product.

If you have fine hair and want to avoid greasy-looking strands, reach for OUAI's scalp serum. "It's lightweight and doesn't make your hair greasy because it has glycerin and hyaluronic acid for moisture delivery," says Dr. Mian. It also has ingredients like red clover flower extract to help soothe an inflamed scalp while it heals. There are hair benefits, too, thanks to peptides that promote fuller, thicker strands.

It is the most costly serum on our list, but users say it's a worthy splurge for those who want something lightweight and effective with the added benefit of a great scent.

When shopping, look for ingredients like glycerin, coconut oil, jojoba oil, or argan oil, says Kiran Mian, MD, a dermatologist at Hudson Dermatology and Laser Surgery. When you have a dry scalp, it's also very important to avoid sulfates. "Sulfates, while great at creating a lather and deep clean, can be drying for the hair and scalp," Dr. Mian says.

Some scalp moisturizers are leave-in products, while others require a wait time before rinsing. Leave-in products tend to be more convenient, since you massage in and then can get on with your routine. However, those with very fine hair may find some leave-in products too heavy. If you're concerned about a scalp serum making your hair look greasy, you may want to consider a rinse-out product, which typically has a wait time of anywhere from 3 to 10 minutes. If you do choose to use a rinse-out product, though, make sure to allot time for washing your hair that day.

To find the best scalp moisturizers to quell itchiness and banish dandruff and white flakes, the Women's Health team consulted two dermatologists and a hair transplant surgeon, plus asked our team of anonymous testers and in-house editors for feedback on the products they use and love. We then put a handful of the top-rated products to the test, evaluating them for attributes like ingredient list, ease of use, and overall efficacy.

#4931. Alibaba's Qwen 4 Max Leads China's AI Agent Race—But You Can't Download It

Alibaba's Qwen 4 Max Leads China's AI Agent Race—But You Can't Download It

Alibaba released Qwen 4 Max on Monday, its most powerful AI model yet and the first flagship built on its new Qwen 4 architecture.

It is also the highest-ranked Chinese model on Arena's agent leaderboard, putting the company ahead of Tencent, Moonshot AI and DeepSeek in that particular test.

The new model has 2.4 trillion parameters, can process text, images and video, and accepts up to one million tokens of context. Parameters are all the different dials a model can handle and tweak when processing information. Tokens are basically the smallest unit of information a model can handle. Its current configuration is enough room for lengthy codebases or stacks of documents.

Alibaba uses a mixture-of-experts design, which keeps most of those parameters idle for any given word it processes. Qwen 4 Max activates 71 billion at a time, compared with 95 billion for Qwen 3.8 Max, allowing a very large model to use less computing power per token.

On Agent Arena, Qwen 4 Max placed 14th among individual models and made Alibaba the fifth-ranked laboratory overall.

The leaderboard evaluates real agent sessions using task completion, user satisfaction and how well models respond to corrections, then scores each model by its net percentage improvement over an average competitor. Qwen 4 Max posted a preliminary 7.46% score across 14,727 sessions, the highest among Chinese entries.

Its visual work may be the more interesting part for regular users. The Code Arena web-development ranking compares websites built by AI models using head-to-head user votes and a points-based rating system. Qwen 4 Max debuted sixth globally at 1,750 points, up 74 from its predecessor, and placed eighth in categories for branding and reference-based design.

That puts it in the same neighborhood as the best American models at turning a request, a screenshot or a rough idea into a working interface that actually looks good.

Alibaba's demos go further, showing the model building game environments and translating factory layouts into 3D models, although those are company-selected examples rather than independent tests.

The visual capability is for understanding images and video and producing code or other text-based outputs. It is not the same as releasing a new image generator.

Qwen 4 Max costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million generated tokens through QwenCloud, a 25% reduction from the previous flagship's $2 and $6 rates. Reused input served from an automatic cache costs $0.075 per million tokens, which can make repetitive workflows substantially cheaper.

Alibaba says its internal testing across hundreds of professional specialties found that the model used 35% fewer tokens and reduced average task costs by roughly 60% compared with Qwen 3.8 Max. In other words, it should be cheaper to execute tasks on this model even against competitors with a similar price..

The bigger limitation for the community is that Qwen 4 Max is closed-weight. Developers can use it through an API or Alibaba's apps, but they cannot download its internal parameters, modify it or run it privately on their own hardware.

Qwen has become a foundation for the open-model ecosystem. An August report from Hugging Face counted 151,448 Qwen-based derivative models on its platform, about 4.7 times the number built specifically on Meta's Llama family. Those include community fine-tunes and optimized versions that power local assistants and specialized tools.

Alibaba opened the weights of Qwen 3.8 Max earlier this year, despite having kept some previous Max models proprietary. It also previewed elements of the Qwen 4 architecture with smaller models months before Monday's release.

The launch lands in a crowded Chinese race. Moonshot's Kimi K3 pushed enormous open-weight models toward Western performance, while DeepSeek has been competing hard on API prices.

Qwen 4 Max leads some Chinese rankings, but American labs still hold the top spots in Arena's overall agent and web-development tables. They are also considerably more expensive.

Alibaba says smaller Qwen 4 models will be released with open weights, giving developers a chance to build on this generation rather than simply rent its biggest model. It has not announced their sizes or release dates.
